answer: Per the Copilot4DevOps page on modernrequirements.com, Copilot4DevOps is offered in three tiers based on monthly AI token allowance: Lite (2M tokens, free), Plus (30M tokens, roughly $30–40/month), and Ultimate (100M tokens, roughly $40–50/month). These figures are as published on the product page and may change — confirm current pricing with Modern Requirements sales.

title: Modern Requirements4DevOps NextGen performance claims vs the 2025 (Classic) version
answer: Per modernrequirements.com's Modern Requirements4DevOps product page, NextGen is described as 60% faster for comparisons, file opens, reports, and traceability versus the MR 2025 (Classic) version, with 90%+ of known issues from the previous version resolved. The page also notes NextGen auto-scales on Azure App Service, removing the need for manual capacity planning.

title: What is AI Edit in Modern Requirements4DevOps
answer: AI Edit, per the Modern Requirements4DevOps product page on modernrequirements.com, is a one-click AI assistance feature accessible from the Azure DevOps context menu. It's aimed at focused, single-item editing and quality checks on individual work items (rather than bulk operations).

title: Which compliance standards is Modern Requirements4DevOps built for
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps's product page on modernrequirements.com states it's "purpose-built" for regulated-industry standards including FDA 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 13485, IEC 62304, DO-178C, ISO 26262, and ASPICE. (For dedicated clause-by-clause compliance tracking and audit-package generation across a broader standards list, see Compliance4DevOps — a separate companion product.)

title: Modern Requirements pricing plans and what's included
answer: Modern Requirements' pricing page (modernrequirements.com/pricing/) lists four packages: Frontier ("the mainline platform"), Frontier AI ("Frontier + AI capabilities," marked Popular), Engineering ("for systems engineering"), and Engineering AI ("Engineering + AI capabilities," marked Popular). All plans include native AI features (Elicitation, Analysis, Convert, Transform) plus Smart Docs, Smart Report, Document Management, Word Import, Test Hub Reporting, Review Management, Trace Analysis, and Baseline. The AI-tier plans (Frontier AI and Engineering AI) add the full AI capability set: Chat, Diagram Generation, Mockup, Pseudocode & Test Scripts, Dynamic Prompt, SOP/Document Generator, Transform, and Q&A Assistant. The Engineering-tier plans (Engineering and Engineering AI) add Variant Management and Parameterized Requirements. The page does not publish specific per-user or subscription prices — it uses "Request Pricing" buttons throughout.

title: Modern Requirements support tiers by plan
answer: Per modernrequirements.com/pricing/, support level differs by plan: Frontier includes Basic Support plus MR Academy access; Frontier AI includes Priority Support plus MR Academy and AI4DevOps Academy access; Engineering AI includes Premium Support plus early access to new features and to Agents4DevOps. This indicates Agents4DevOps is currently being rolled out as an early-access feature for Engineering AI customers rather than being generally available on all plans.

title: Where to find self-study videos, tutorials, and learning resources for Modern Requirements4DevOps
answer: Modern Requirements' Help Center / learning hub (modernrequirements.com/resources/help-center/) hosts a 4-week "Bootcamp" video series covering requirements-workflow fundamentals, plus text-based Product Tutorials on Smart Docs, Traceability, Smart Report, Review Management, Baseline, and Document Management (these overlap with the feature documentation already covered in the NextGen Online Help). It also links to blog articles (including industry-specific guides for standards like GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, DO-178C, DO-254, and ASPICE), gated whitepapers (DO-254, DO-178C, Data Dictionaries, AS9100, ISO 13485) that require a download/form submission, and recorded webinars on compliance, AI, and healthcare topics.

title: What is MR Academy and how do you enroll
answer: MR Academy is Modern Requirements' free Learning Management System offering self-paced courses and certifications in requirements management and Azure DevOps, at modernrequirements.com/mr-academy/. Enrollment is a three-step process that requires entering the activation key "Learn" (case-sensitive). Featured certification courses listed on the page are: AI Powered Requirements, Smart Reporting, Trace Analysis, Document Authoring, Use Case Management, and Impact Assessment — each with a "Register to get certified" link.

title: What are acceptance criteria (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary (modernrequirements.com/glossary/): Acceptance criteria are "the specific, testable conditions a user story or requirement must meet to be considered complete."

title: What is an Azure DevOps work item (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: An Azure DevOps work item is "a record used to track a single piece of work, such as a user story, bug, task, feature, or epic."

title: What is change impact analysis (Glossary)
keywords: what does change impact analysis mean
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Change impact analysis is "the process of working out what a proposed change to a requirement will affect before the change is made."

title: What is EARS notation (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: EARS notation stands for "Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax — a set of simple sentence templates for writing clear, testable requirements."

title: What is an Epic in Azure DevOps (Glossary)
keywords: what does epic mean in azure devops
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: An Epic is "the highest level of work item in Azure DevOps, representing a large body of work that spans multiple features and often several months."

title: What is a Feature work item in Azure DevOps (Glossary)
keywords: what is a feature in azure devops
what does feature mean azure devops
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A Feature is "a mid-level work item in Azure DevOps that represents a distinct capability a product delivers, sitting below an epic and above user stories."

title: What are functional requirements (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Functional requirements are "descriptions of something a product must do — a specific behavior, feature, or response to a given input."

title: What are non-functional requirements (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Non-functional requirements are "requirements that define how well a system must perform rather than what it does, covering qualities like speed, security, reliability, scalability, and usability."

title: What is a product backlog (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A product backlog is "an ordered list of everything a team might work on for a product, from features and user stories to fixes and improvements."

title: What is requirements analysis (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements analysis is "the work of examining gathered requirements to ensure they are clear, complete, consistent, and feasible, then prioritizing and refining them."

title: What is a requirements baseline (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A requirements baseline is "a reviewed and approved set of requirements, frozen at a point in time to serve as the agreed reference for the work ahead."

title: What is requirements elicitation (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements elicitation is "the work of drawing out what stakeholders actually need, using techniques like interviews, workshops, observation, and prototyping."

title: What is requirements engineering (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements engineering is "the discipline of discovering, analyzing, documenting, validating, and managing the requirements for a system across its lifecycle."

title: What is requirements gathering (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements gathering is "the process of collecting the needs and expectations for a product from stakeholders, users, and other sources at the start of a project."

title: What is requirements management (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements management is "the process of documenting, organizing, and tracking a product's requirements across its lifecycle, so that stakeholder needs are captured, agreed on, and traceable."

title: What is requirements management in Azure DevOps (Glossary)
keywords: what is requirements management in azure devops
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements management in Azure DevOps is "the practice of capturing, organizing, and tracing requirements directly inside Azure DevOps, using work items like epics, features, and user stories."

title: What is a requirements management plan (Glossary)
keywords: what is a requirements management plan
what does requirements management plan mean
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A requirements management plan is "a document that sets out how requirements will be handled on a project — how they are captured, tracked, changed, and traced, and who is responsible."

title: What is a requirements review (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A requirements review is "a structured check of requirements by stakeholders to confirm they are clear, complete, correct, and agreed before development starts."

title: What is requirements traceability (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements traceability is "the practice of linking each requirement to its source and to everything downstream that fulfills or verifies it, such as designs, code, and test cases."

title: What is a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) is "a table that maps each requirement to the items that satisfy and verify it, such as design elements, test cases, and results."

title: What is requirements versioning (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Requirements versioning is "the practice of tracking changes to requirements over time, keeping a record of what changed, when, and by whom."

title: What is a Software Requirements Specification (SRS) (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A Software Requirements Specification (SRS) is "a document that describes what a software system must do and the constraints it must work within."

title: What is test case management in Azure DevOps (Glossary)
keywords: test case management in azure devops
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Test case management in Azure DevOps is "the practice of creating, organizing, and running test cases within Azure Test Plans, and linking them to requirements and user stories."

title: What is traceability in Azure DevOps (Glossary)
keywords: what does traceability mean azure devops
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Traceability in Azure DevOps is "linking work items to each other and to code, builds, and tests, so a team can follow a requirement through to the work that delivers and verifies it."

title: What is a use case (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A use case is "a description of how a user or another system interacts with a system to achieve a specific goal, laid out as a sequence of steps."

title: What is a user story (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: A user story is "a short, plain-language description of a feature told from the point of view of the person who wants it," typically in the form "as a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]."

title: What is verification and validation (V&V) (Glossary)
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: Verification and validation (V&V) are "two complementary checks on a product — verification confirms the product meets specifications, while validation confirms it meets stakeholder needs."

title: What is the work item hierarchy (Epic, Feature, Story) (Glossary)
keywords: what is the work item hierarchy
answer: Per the Modern Requirements Glossary: The work item hierarchy (Epic, Feature, Story) is "the parent-child structure in Azure DevOps that organizes work from broad to specific, typically Epic at the top, then Feature, then User Story, then Task."

title: Reaching the License Activation Page on the Standalone version
answer: For the Standalone version (as opposed to the Embedded version inside Azure DevOps/TFS), reach the License Activation page by opening a browser and navigating to http://[hostname]:8028/User/SignIn (replace [hostname] with your server name), then click Sign In. If the system has not yet been activated, you'll be redirected to the License Activation Page, where you can choose User Based, Floating, or Offline Activation as usual.

title: Favorites Tab (personal quick-access bookmarks)
answer: Every module in MR4DevOps Frontier has a Browse page (the main listing view for documents, matrices, packages, baselines, and reports), and at the top of each Browse page is a Favorites tab — a personal quick-access area. Mark any item as a favorite and it appears there, saving you from scrolling through long lists to find something you use regularly. Favorites are personal to your account: each user maintains their own set independently of colleagues, and items can be added or removed at any time.

title: ADO-Style Filter Panel
keywords: search work item type state assigned to
answer: Every module in MR4DevOps Frontier includes an ADO-style filter panel, available on the Browse page and main views. It supports multiple search criteria at once — work item type, state, assigned-to, tags, and more — in a layout that mirrors Azure DevOps's own filtering, so it feels familiar with no learning curve. This works whether you're searching documents, a traceability matrix, a version package, or a baseline. Filters can be combined and adjusted freely, and the panel collapses when not in use to keep the workspace uncluttered.

title: Smart Edit — unified work item editing window
answer:
Smart Edit is MR4DevOps Frontier's unified work item editing experience: everything needed to view, edit, and manage a work item lives in a single organized window, so you never have to jump between screens. You can edit all work item fields directly, manage Links and Attachments through dedicated editable tabs, and open Linked Artifacts from its own tab for structured cross-item navigation. A Variants Hierarchy tab gives a visual overview of related variants, Tags and Discussion fields are shown inline, and Up/Down navigation arrows let you move through work items in sequence without reopening each one. When editing HTML fields, use @ to mention team members and # to reference other work items, matching the native Azure DevOps experience.

Note: this is distinct from the Smart View side-by-side revision/variant comparison feature, which is a separate capability that also lives under the Smart Edit/Smart View name.

title: Smart Report — automated document and report generation
answer: Smart Report is the reporting engine built into both Smart Docs and Traceability (this is separate from the Reporting/Advanced Reports module, which is for reports built from scratch). Select a template and stylesheet, preview the output, and export as Word, PDF, or HTML — or save directly to the Document Management Library. Templates are created and customized in a built-in Designer tab, where you choose which work item types, fields, and sections to include. Organizations that need branded or regulated document formats can upload custom .dotx Word templates instead of using the built-in ones.

title: AI Edit — the four editing modes and Ask Anything chat
answer: AI Edit's panel presents four structured modes on its left side: Explore and Review Work Item Content (understand what's already in the item), Edit Descriptions and Details (update and improve field content with AI assistance), Refine Specific Sections (target one particular area for refinement), and Get AI-Powered Suggestions (receive proactive improvement recommendations). Below these is a free-form "Ask Anything" chat input for a direct conversation with the AI about the selected work item — requesting rewrites, adjusting reading level, changing length, adding acceptance criteria, or applying polish, all without switching tools. Edits are saved back to ADO with the Save Changes button. AI Edit is meant for quick, in-context assistance on one work item at a time, as opposed to opening the full Copilot4DevOps interface.

title: ADO Context Menu — available quick-launch actions
keywords: send for review from context menu
what actions are in the ado context menu
answer: MR4DevOps Frontier adds a group of its own actions into the Azure DevOps work item context menu (right-click a work item in a backlog, board, or query result list, or use the ⋮ options menu). The available actions are: Copilot4DevOps (launch the full AI assistant), AI Edit (open the AI work item editor), Smart Edit (open the side pane to update work item fields), Smart Report (generate a report for the selected item), Send for Review (start a formal review request), Create Package (create a Version Package from the selected items), Create Baseline (capture a baseline snapshot), and Reuse Work Items (copy the selected items into an existing baseline in the current project). This lets you kick off any of these workflows without navigating away from wherever you're already working in Azure DevOps.

title: Agent4DevOps — AI agent automation and governance platform
answer:
Agent4DevOps (also referred to as Agents4DevOps) is MR4DevOps Frontier's end-to-end platform for configuring, running, and governing AI agents across DevOps projects. Its core workspaces: a Jobs tab is the master execution history, where every agent run appears as a filterable job with status, credit-usage dashboards, and controls to refresh, terminate, or delete runs; a Job Explorer gives a deep dive into individual runs (run details, agent responses, interactive approval tasks, an integrated chat assistant). The Agents workspace shows all system and custom agents in a filterable grid, and supports creating two kinds: execution agents (built from natural-language instructions, uploaded code/config, or library templates) and assisted autonomous agents (built with AI, manually, or from templates, with configurable triggers, approvals, tools, and notifications). A Skills tab centralizes reusable capabilities agents draw on, and a Library provides prebuilt agents and skills to start from instead of building everything from scratch.

Governance lives in the Admin Panel: administrators define how agents connect to backend services (personal access tokens, base URLs), configure outbound email (SMTP or SendGrid, with test emails and audit logs), and set daily credit-consumption alerts that can automatically disable the highest-consuming agents to protect the monthly quota. They can also assign prioritized AI models per module (with fallbacks), pick a consistent Chat Assistant model, and use a Global Tool Call section to enable/disable specific agent capabilities. A permission model covers twelve key actions (managing, deleting, executing, and enabling agents/skills, plus job and task operations) both globally and per project, with inheritance and allow/deny/not-set options.

title: Test Case Management — the five Virtual Work Items and Virtual Linking
keywords: virtual work items test case management
requirement category test point test run test result test step run
answer: Azure DevOps's native testing hierarchy (Test Plan → Test Suite → Test Case) covers basic organization but doesn't capture who ran which test, the outcome at each step, or which bugs were raised. MR4DevOps Frontier's Test Case Management extends this through five Virtual Work Items: Requirement Category, Test Point, Test Run, Test Result, and Test Step Run. These sit alongside your real ADO work items and are connected through Virtual Linking, giving a complete end-to-end view of the test lifecycle — from the original requirement down to the individual test step outcome and any bugs filed — without changing your existing ADO process. All of this virtual work item data feeds directly into the Traceability and Smart Report modules for compliance-ready test reporting, and Test Results support multiple iterations, screen recordings, and user action log attachments.

title: Review — Approve All/Reject All and Response panel filters
keywords: response panel filter my response all responses all comments summary
answer: In the Review module, reviewers work through assigned items one by one, adding comments and submitting a response before clicking Mark as Reviewed. Approvers can Approve or Reject individual items, or act on the full set at once with Approve All or Reject All — any rejection requires a comment, creating an automatic audit trail. Recipients access their assigned reviews directly from a "Reviews Assigned To Me" queue without needing to navigate to the source document. The Response panel can be filtered to show: your own responses (My Response), all reviewer feedback (All Responses), all comments (All Comments), or a full Summary — making it easy for the request owner to track progress and close out the review.

title: Traceability — Grid, List, and Heatmap views and coverage colors
keywords: traceability matrix grid view list view heatmap view
answer: Once a Traceability matrix is generated (via Intersection Matrix, mapping two work item types against each other, or Horizontal Matrix, expanding a linked hierarchy), the Traceability Matrix tab offers three views: Grid View shows a compact two-dimensional grid with checkmark cells where links exist and lets you add/remove links directly; List View shows each row as a card with linked items as chips and flags uncovered items with an N/A badge; Heatmap View shows a color-coded coverage bar per row — Grey (0%), Teal (1–49%), Orange (50–79%), Green (80–100%). An Analytics tab provides gap analysis by work item type, overall coverage percentage, and state distribution.

title: Baseline — merging, copying to another project, and the Difference Report
keywords: reuse work items from existing baseline
answer: Beyond simply capturing a point-in-time snapshot, Baseline in MR4DevOps Frontier supports: copying a baseline to another project, reusing work items from an existing baseline into a new one, and merging two baselines into one consolidated baseline. The Compare tab shows the current state of all constituent work items against the baseline, or against another baseline directly. A Difference Report can be generated from any comparison — a structured Word document recording every change — which the guide describes as an essential tool for regulated industries that need formal change records. A baseline itself is immutable once captured and cannot be altered.

title: Version Package — variants, color-coded comparison, and locking
keywords: color-coded diff added changed removed moved
answer: Version Package groups related work items into a managed, versioned package (typically a release, system configuration, or requirements set), built from a query that auto-populates its work items. Packages support variants — parallel configurations of the same requirement set for different products, regions, or customer targets. The key capability is comparison: compare a package against a previous version with a color-coded difference view (added, changed, removed, moved), or compare a package against one of its variants side by side. Packages can be locked at key milestones to prevent unintended changes, and a Variants tab shows all source/target variant relationships.

title: Admin Panel tabs (Frontier, 2026 edition)
answer:
In the 2026 Frontier edition, the Admin Panel (Azure DevOps Organization Settings → the MR4DevOps Frontier section, Collection Administrators only) is structured into: a Licensing tab (current license status and seat allocation), a General tab (organization-wide settings applying to all modules), and dedicated configuration tabs for Smart Docs, Baseline, Review, and Copilot4DevOps, each exposing that module's own settings and defaults (field requirements, default templates, integration options, which features are enabled for end users).

Note: this is the current Frontier tab set. An older description of the Admin Panel (from the Admin Configuration Guide) lists seven sections instead — the tab set has evolved between versions, so check which edition you're on if the tabs you see don't match one of these lists.

title: Copilot4DevOps — the four capability groups
keywords: refine and convert elicit analyze convert transform
assistant and support chat qa impact assessment
advanced tools generate dynamic prompt sop document generator
answer: MR4DevOps Frontier organizes Copilot4DevOps's functions into four capability groups. Refine and Convert: Elicit (generate backlog/test items from requirements), Analyze (evaluate requirements against 6C's, INVEST, and MoSCoW frameworks), Convert (express requirements as user stories or use cases), and Transform (summarize, paraphrase, elaborate, or translate content). Visualize and Design: Diagram (visual requirement diagrams) and Mockup (instant UI wireframe generation). Assistant and Support: a conversational Chat interface, a Q&A Assistant that elicits detailed requirements through structured questions, and an Impact Assessment tool for evaluating how a proposed change affects existing work items. Advanced Tools: Generate (requirements into pseudocode, test scripts, or AI specs), Dynamic Prompt (custom templates for repeatable AI workflows), and SOP/Document Generator (structured documents in seconds). It's accessible from Smart Docs, Version Package, and the ADO work item context menu, and all capabilities operate on your live ADO data.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — prerequisites before installing
answer: Before installing Copilot4DevOps on-premises (v9), the server needs: the IIS Web Server role (Windows Server Roles) with Web Socket enabled through Windows Features; the WebDAV Common HTTP Feature uninstalled if present, followed by a restart; the IIS URL Rewrite module installed and visible in IIS's Web Server section; Microsoft ASP.NET Core Runtime 10.0.x (the Hosting Bundle) — uninstall any older 8.0.x Hosting Bundle first; the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable package-2022 (restart the system after installing this); and MongoDB version 7.0.2 or later. Virtualization Technology (VT-x) must also be enabled and supported on the server, since Copilot4DevOps requires a Docker-based Redis Stack Server running via WSL2 — if the server is a cloud virtual machine, nested virtualization must be enabled too. Copilot4DevOps v9 supports Azure DevOps Server 2022 and later versions.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — enabling WSL2 and installing Docker Desktop
keywords: wsl 2 based engine instead of hyper-v
answer: To prepare a Windows Server for the Redis Stack Server Copilot4DevOps needs: in an elevated PowerShell, run `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux -NoRestart`, then `-FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform -NoRestart`, then `-FeatureName Containers -All -NoRestart`, and restart the computer (`Restart-Computer`) — don't skip the restart. Next, install the WSL2 kernel update (wsl_update_x64.msi), then in an elevated PowerShell run `wsl --update` followed by `wsl --set-default-version 2`. Finally, install Docker Desktop for Windows, choosing "Use WSL 2 based engine instead of Hyper-V" during setup, log out and back in, launch Docker Desktop, and confirm it's working with `docker version` (you should see both Client and Server details in the output).

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — installing Redis Stack Server via Docker
answer:
With Docker Desktop running, pull the image with `docker pull redis/redis-stack-server:latest`. Create a host folder for persistence, e.g. `mkdir C:\redis\redis-data`. Then run the container: `docker run -d --name redis-stack -p 6379:6379 -v "C:/redis/redis-data:/data" --restart always redis/redis-stack-server:latest redis-stack-server --requirepass "redispass" --dir /data` (change the password from the example). This runs Redis Stack on port 6379 with the host directory mounted for persistence. Confirm it's running with `docker ps`.

Note: if Copilot4DevOps is being installed on a server that already runs Modern Requirements4DevOps (which has its own Redis on 6379), map Redis Stack to a different host port instead — e.g. `-p 6079:6379` — to avoid a port conflict, and use that port in Copilot4DevOps's own connection string.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — installing MongoDB 7.0.2 (fresh install)
answer: For a server with no existing MongoDB, download the MongoDB 7.0.2 MSI installer (mongodb-windows-x86_64-7.0.2-signed.msi) and run it choosing Complete installation. Install the MongoDB service running as the Network Service user, keeping the default Service Name and data/log directories. Optionally select Install MongoDB Compass for a GUI to browse the database, then finish the wizard.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — running a second MongoDB instance alongside an existing one
keywords: install mongod as a service uncheck
answer: If the server already runs Modern Requirements4DevOps with its own MongoDB (on the default port 27017), install Copilot4DevOps's required MongoDB 7.0.2 as a second, separate instance rather than replacing the existing one. In the MongoDB installer, choose Custom/Advanced installation and uncheck "Install MongoD as a Service" (don't let the installer register it automatically). Create separate data and log folders (e.g. C:\Program Files\MongoDB\dbv7 and \logv7). In an elevated Command Prompt, register it manually on a different port: `"C:\Program Files\MongoDB\Server\7.0\bin\mongod.exe" --dbpath="C:\Program Files\MongoDB\dbv7" --logpath="C:\Program Files\MongoDB\logv7\mongod.log" --port 21018 --install --serviceName "MongoDBv7" --serviceDisplayName "MongoDBv7"`, then start it with `net start MongoDBv7`. Verify both services in services.msc: the original MongoDB on 27017 (used by ModernRequirements4DevOps) and MongoDBv7 on 21018 (used by Copilot4DevOps), both set to start automatically.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — deploying the files and creating the IIS site
keywords: net clr version integrated pipeline mode
answer: Download the latest Copilot4DevOps package from the link provided by the Modern Requirements Support team, and extract it to the IIS web server location (e.g. C:\Inetpub\Copilot4DevOps). In IIS Manager, create a new Application Pool for Copilot4DevOps (.NET CLR version and Integrated managed pipeline mode as required), then open its Advanced Settings and set Enable 32-Bit Applications to False. Add a new Website with that site name, application pool, and physical path, choosing HTTPS (or HTTP, depending on your organization's requirements) as the binding type, with the appropriate host name and SSL certificate.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — configuring appsettings.json connection strings
answer: In the deployed Copilot4DevOps folder's appsettings.json, point every connection setting at your MongoDB and Redis instances: Database → ConnectionString and DBName, FileStorage → Mongo ConnectionString, SemanticKernel's ChatHistory and FilesPersistence database connection strings, VectorStore's Redis connection string (format: `<host>:<port>,password=<password>,abortConnect=false`), Cache → ConnectionString, and the Logging section's Target/MongoDB connection string — all normally `mongodb://localhost:<port>` for MongoDB, or `<host>:<port>,password=...` for the VectorStore/Redis entry. When Copilot4DevOps shares a server with an existing Modern Requirements4DevOps install, these ports must point at Copilot4DevOps's own separate MongoDB/Redis instances (e.g. mongodb://localhost:21018 and localhost:6079), not the ones ModernRequirements4DevOps already uses (27017 and 6379) — using the same ports/database names for both products isn't supported and will cause conflicts.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — SSL certificate thumbprint and Allowed Domains
answer: Copilot4DevOps's appsettings.json needs the site's SSL certificate thumbprint in ByPassSSLThumbprints, and the site's domain name in AllowedDomains. To get the thumbprint: in IIS Manager, open the site's bindings, click Edit, then View on the SSL certificate, and copy the value from the "Thumbprint" field on the Details tab — or in PowerShell, run `Get-ChildItem -Path cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where-Object { $_.Subject -eq "CN=<your-domain>" }` (replace `<your-domain>` with your certificate's domain name) and copy the Thumbprint column. Paste the thumbprint into ByPassSSLThumbprints in uppercase, and add the site's domain to AllowedDomains — multiple entries for either setting are separated with a pipe (`|`) character.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — unlocking WebSocket and restarting IIS
keywords: net stop was net start w3svc
answer: Copilot4DevOps needs the WebSocket configuration section unlocked in IIS. In an elevated Command Prompt, run: `%windir%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd unlock config /section:system.webServer/webSocket`. Then restart IIS's services: `net stop was /y` followed by `net start w3svc`. These two steps unlock WebSocket support and bring IIS back up with the change applied — do this after configuring appsettings.json and before testing the site.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — verifying the deployment worked
answer: After deploying and configuring the site, open its URL in a browser (from IIS Manager's "Browse Website" action, or the URL you bound it to). A working deployment shows a plain-text confirmation like "Copilot4DevOps vX.X (Build: v0.x.x.x) application is running." with a multilingual-mode status line — this page appearing means IIS, the app pool, and the appsettings.json connections are all correctly wired up. From there, log into your Azure DevOps account and exercise the actual Copilot4DevOps functionality (or check the About section for the version) to confirm it's fully working, not just that the site responds.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — upgrading from v6 (or later) to v9
keywords: stop and remove iis site before upgrade
skip wsl docker steps already configured
uninstall old net core runtime before upgrade
answer:
To upgrade an existing on-premises Copilot4DevOps from v6 or later to v9: confirm the current install is fully functional with MongoDB 7.x+ first, verify Web Socket is enabled in IIS, uninstall the WebDAV Common HTTP Feature if present (restart after), and make sure IIS URL Rewrite is installed. Uninstall the older Microsoft ASP.NET Core Runtime 8.0.x Hosting Bundle and install .NET Core 10.0.x in its place, and confirm the Visual C++ Redistributable 2022 package is present. Then in IIS Manager stop the Copilot4DevOps site and remove it, and rename the existing install folder (e.g. C:\Inetpub\Copilot4DevOps → C:\Inetpub\Copilot4DevOpsOld, or append the old version number) rather than deleting it.

If the server's current setup already uses a Docker-based Redis Stack Server, an external Ubuntu Server VM running Redis Stack Server, or WSL-based Ubuntu with Redis Stack Server, you can skip the WSL/Docker/Redis Stack setup steps entirely and go straight to redeploying the files (extract the new v9 package to the original path), recreating the IIS site, and updating appsettings.json's connection strings, SSL thumbprint, and allowed domains the same way as a fresh install. Only servers upgrading from a version earlier than v6 need to go through the full WSL/Docker/Redis Stack setup from scratch. Copilot4DevOps v9 requires Azure DevOps Server 2022 or later.

title: Integrating Copilot4DevOps with an existing Modern Requirements4DevOps install
answer: When Copilot4DevOps and Modern Requirements4DevOps run on the same server as separate IIS sites, MR4DevOps needs to be told where to find Copilot4DevOps. In IIS Manager, open the Copilot4DevOps site and copy its URL from the Browse Website panel. Then select the Modern Requirements4DevOps site, open Application Settings, and edit the Copilot4DevOps.ApplicationUrl property, setting its value to the URL you just copied. Restart the IIS web server for the change to take effect, then confirm the integration by using a Copilot4DevOps-powered feature from within Modern Requirements4DevOps.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — allowing the PUT verb in IIS Handler Mappings and Request Filtering
keywords: request filtering http verbs allow put
answer: Copilot4DevOps needs the PUT HTTP verb allowed in two separate IIS settings on its site, or certain requests will fail. First, in IIS Manager, open the Copilot4DevOps site's Handler Mappings, find ExtensionlessUrlHandler-Integrated-4.0, double-click it, click Request Restrictions, switch to the Verbs tab, and either select "All verbs" or select "One of the following verbs" and explicitly append `,PUT` to the list (e.g. `GET,HEAD,POST,DEBUG,PUT`). Second, open Request Filtering on the same site, go to the HTTP Verbs tab: if PUT is listed with Allowed = False, right-click it and choose Remove; if it isn't listed at all, click Allow Verb and add PUT.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — setting the MR_COPILOT_ENCRYPTION environment variables on the app pool
keywords: set environment variables copilot4devops app pool
answer: Copilot4DevOps's application pool needs four encryption-related environment variables set directly on it. In an elevated Command Prompt, run `cd C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv`, then use `appcmd set config -section:system.applicationHost/applicationPools /+"[name='Copilot4DevOps'].environmentVariables.[name='<VAR_NAME>',value='<value>']" /commit:apphost` once each for MR_COPILOT_ENCRYPTION_LEGACY_KEY, MR_COPILOT_ENCRYPTION_LEGACY_IVHEX, MR_COPILOT_ENCRYPTION_UTILITY_AESKEY, and MR_COPILOT_ENCRYPTION_UTILITY_AESIV (use the exact values provided for your deployment, not placeholders), then run `appcmd recycle apppool /apppool.name:"Copilot4DevOps"` to apply them. Because these commands are long, paste them into Notepad first and check they haven't been split or line-wrapped incorrectly before copying each one into Command Prompt — a broken command here is a common cause of the app pool failing to pick up the keys.

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — starting Docker automatically after a server reboot
keywords: docker not running after server restart
redis stack not running after reboot
auto start docker desktop windows server
answer: Since Copilot4DevOps depends on the Redis Stack Server container, Docker Desktop needs to come back up automatically whenever the server reboots — it doesn't do this on its own by default. Create a Windows Task Scheduler task (taskschd.msc): on the General tab, run whether the user is logged on or not, with highest privileges; on the Triggers tab, trigger "At startup" with a ~30 second delay (to avoid conflicting with other services still starting); on the Actions tab, start a program pointing at Docker Desktop's executable (e.g. `"C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`); on the Conditions tab, uncheck all the idle/power/network conditions; and on the Settings tab, allow the task to run on demand, run it as soon as possible after a missed start, retry every 5 minutes up to 3 attempts on failure, and force-stop it if it doesn't end when requested. After saving, restart the server and confirm both the scheduled task ran (Task Scheduler's Last Run Result) and the Redis Stack container is up (`docker ps` in PowerShell).

title: Copilot4DevOps on-premises — generating and installing the Copilot4DevOps extension in Azure DevOps Server
keywords: deploy copilot4devops extension azure devops server
upload extension manage extensions azure devops server
get it free copilot4devops azure boards
install copilot4devops extension team project collection
answer:
After deploying the Copilot4DevOps web application itself, it still needs to be installed as an extension in Azure DevOps Server (on-premises only) before it shows up on Azure Boards. Run the Extension Maker executable (provided by the Modern Requirements team), enter the Copilot4DevOps site's URL when prompted, and generate the .vsix package (edevtech-mr.CoPilot4DevOps-x.x.x.vsix) — save it somewhere secure.

Then, signed in to Azure DevOps Server as an account with permission to install extensions: open the Marketplace icon → Manage Extensions → Browse local extensions → Manage Extensions (button) → Upload Extension, and upload the .vsix file. Once it's installed, refresh Browse Local Extensions, select the CoPilot4DevOps tile, click "Get it free", choose the Team Project Collection to install it into, and click Install. Once done, the extension appears on the Azure Boards tiles for that collection, and opening it shows the Copilot4DevOps chat screen (Chat, Elicit, Analyze, Impact Assessment, etc.).

keywords: document management audit trail download functionality
answer:
(Document Management module, MR 2.0 / NextGen)

Steps:

2. Find the meatball icon situated beside the "New Folder" option.
3. Click on the meatball icon and select the 'Download Audit Trail' option.
4. The download of the audit trail for the specific project will begin.
   Understanding the Audit Trail Report
   The audit trail report is an essential tool for monitoring user activities and project modifications, presented in a well-structured Excel file consisting of two informative sheets:
1. Introduction Sheet
   The Introduction Sheet provides a summary that includes the report name, project collection URL, creator details, and the report generation timestamp, ensuring clarity and accountability.
   Report Name
   Document User Trail
   Project Collection URL
   URL of the project collection
   Created By
   Name of the user who generated the report
   Created Date
   Date and time when the report was generated (shown in UTC and according to admin settings)
2. Audit Trail Sheet
   The Audit Trail Sheet captures all logged events, organized with the most recent changes at the top, detailing critical information such as project ID, project name, the actor involved, event timestamp, action category, and a concise description of each event.
   Project ID
   GUID of the project
   Project Name
   Name of the project
   Actor
   Display name and domain of the individual who triggered the event
   Timestamp
   Time of the event (UTC and admin settings)
   Category
   Type of action (Modify, Create, Delete, Rename)
   Details
   Brief description of the event
   Event Categories
   Our audit trail report serves as a vital resource for meticulously tracking changes within the project, ensuring that every modification is documented for transparency and accountability. This report categorizes events into four key types: Modify, which records any changes made to existing files; Create, highlighting instances where new files are added or uploaded; Delete, capturing the removal of files; and Rename, documenting instances where files undergo renaming. By systematically categorizing these events, we provide a clear and comprehensive view of project activities, empowering teams to maintain control over their data and enhancing the integrity of the project management process.
   Modify
   Changes made to a file
   Create
   A file was created or uploaded
   Delete
   A file was deleted
   Rename
   A file was renamed
   Project Renaming
   In the event that a project is renamed, the audit trail report will accurately reflect the updated project name for all subsequent operations. This ensures that all future entries and activities associated with the project are consistent with the new designation. However, it is important to note that previous operations will continue to display the original project name, thereby preserving a clear historical record of all actions taken prior to the renaming. This approach allows for both clarity in current project references and accountability in tracking the project's evolution over time.

title: Chat
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help)

Accessing Chat in Copilot4DevOps
In Copilot4DevOps, the chat feature can be accessed in two different ways depending on whether you need contextual assistance or a more open-ended interaction. The first method is through a specific work item. By opening a work item from the backlog and launching the Copilot panel, you can select the chat option. This approach provides a contextual chat experience, where the selected work item serves as background information. This context helps Chat better understand your prompts and generate responses that are relevant to the task or issue you're addressing.
The second method is to access the Chat as hub, which functions as a standalone module independent of any specific work item. In this mode, there is no inherited context or reference, so you must provide all relevant information in your prompt. While both methods offer the same core chat functionality, the key difference is that one includes contextual awareness from the start, while the other requires you to start from scratch.
For example, the prompt "Fetch me the description of the selected work item" won't work for the context-free Chat. The user will have to write "Fetch me the description of Work Item ID: 1093"
Apart from the difference in how context is initialized, the functionality of the chat remains consistent with the existing Copilot4DevOps popup experience. Users will still benefit from the same intelligent assistance, response generation, and integration capabilities as before. The choice between the two depends on whether you prefer Chat option to work with existing background data or if you want to initiate a fresh, context-free interaction.

Steps:
1. Invoking the Chat Function Using a Work Item to be Used as a Context
1. Select a work item in your Azure DevOps project and click on the Copilot4DevOps option.
2. In the Copilot window, click on the Chat icon to activate the chat interface.
2. Invoking Chat as a dedicated Hub (Without Context)
1. Navigate to Azure Boards.
2. A new entry point titled "Copilot4DevOps" has been added under the Boards section of the navigation menu. By selecting this option, users will be able to launch the Copilot Chat interface immediately, without needing to initiate it from an individual work item.
   A Few Notable Differences in the UI
1. In the toolbar of the Chat hub, users won't see Smart Prompt option.
2. A News & Tips option has been added in the dedicated Chat hub toolbar that will offer news and tips exclusively regarding the Chat feature.
3. With in the settings icon, users will now see many other options in the standalone Copilot4DevOps Chat.
   Restrictions
• Only users with an Ultimate license can access the chat feature. Verify your subscription.

title: Chat UI
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "Chat")

Understanding the Chat feature's interface is essential for navigating effectively and making the most out it. This guide walks you through each UI component.
The Main Chat Interface
When you open the Chat feature, your screen is divided into two main areas: a navigation sidebar on the left and a chat prompt window on the right.
Using the Sidebar (Left Panel)
All actions such as starting new conversations, searching old ones, and managing chats are handled from the sidebar.
Sidebar Collapse & Expand
Right next to the Copilot4DevOps icon is a toggle button. Clicking this will collapse the sidebar, allowing the prompt window to expand for better visibility.
To reopen it, simply hover your mouse over the Copilot4DevOps icon, and the sidebar icon appears which you can click to expand it again.
Search Option
Click on Search to open a popup and search through your previous chat interactions.

Cloning a text block allows you to create an exact copy of an existing text block under a new name. This is useful when you want to reuse an existing description or setup but make slight modifications. Cloning preserves the original tags and description but allows you to modify these elements in the new text block.
Follow these steps to clone a text block:

   Note: The name should not contain spaces or special characters. If you try to enter spaces or special characters, a notification will appear with the message: "Space and Special characters cannot be entered in the Name field.")
   Example: If you're cloning "WelcomeMessage", you could name the clone "WelcomeMessageV2" or "WelcomeMessageClone".
   The text block is cloned.
   The description of the original text block will be copied into the new cloned text block. If you need to make changes to the description, you can edit it in the Description field.
   The cloned text block will be saved automatically.
7. Click on the "Done" button to close the Text Block Management window.

title: Baseline Comparison Mode
keywords: compare baseline – consider link comparison as global vs context
answer:
(Admin Panel module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Font Settings in Smart Edit")

In the Baseline Compare tab, the work item link comparison can be viewed in two ways:
• Global comparison
• Context comparison
In Global Comparison, a work item will be considered as changed if it encounters a change in the link (created/updated/deleted) with any work item irrespective of whether the work item exists in baseline compare context or outside the context.
Whereas, with Context Comparison, a work item will only be considered as changed if it encounters a change in the link (created/updated/deleted) with a work item that exists in the baseline compare context. The 'Baseline Compare Context' means that all the work items which are showing up under baseline compare tab during the comparison.
The link comparison is supported in all of the three comparison types:

Steps:
1. Comparing a baseline with current version
2. Comparing with another baseline
3. Comparing with a query
   Configuring the toggle button
   In the Baseline compare tab, a toggle button is provided having "Context Comparison for Links" option in it so that users can see the context-based comparison, if required. The toggle button will be shown on UI if configured from the admin panel.
   Here's how you can configure the toggle button:
1. Go to General tab in organization settings. By default, the Global link comparison option is selected. To enable Context Comparison, deselect this option.
2. Select "Show 'Context Comparison' toggle button in baseline compare tab" and click on Save Changes.
3. The toggle button is hidden by default. Once it is configured from the admin panel, the toggle button for link comparison appears at the baseline compare tab.
   When the toggle button is set to ON, it enables Context Comparison and, when it is set to OFF, the default Global Comparison functionality is applied. If the user has set context comparison for links to "ON", it will retain the selection throughout the session. Once the session expires, the functionality will automatically be set as per the configured admin panel settings.

title: Context Based Link Comparison
answer:
(Baseline module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Details Tab")

In the Baseline Compare tab, the work item link comparison can be viewed in two ways:
• Global comparison
• Context comparison
In Global Comparison, a work item will be considered as changed if it encounters a change in the link (created/updated/deleted) with any work item irrespective of whether the work item exists in baseline compare context or outside the context.
Whereas, with Context Comparison, a work item will only be considered as changed if it encounters a change in the link (created/updated/deleted) with a work item that exists in the baseline compare context. The 'Baseline Compare Context' means that all the work items which are showing up under baseline compare tab during the comparison.
The link comparison is supported in all of the three comparison types:

Steps:
1. Comparing a baseline with current version
2. Comparing with another baseline
3. Comparing with a query
   Configuring the toggle button
   In the Baseline compare tab, a toggle button is provided having "Context Comparison for Links"option in it so that users can see the context-based comparison, if required. The toggle button will be shown on UI if configured from the admin panel.
   Here's how you can configure the toggle button:
1. Go to General tab in organization settings. By default, Global link comparison option is selected. To enable Context Comparison, deselect this option.
2. Select "Show 'Context Comparison' toggle button in baseline compare tab" and click on Save Changes.
   Link Comparison Toggle Button
   The toggle button is hidden by default. Once it is configured from the admin panel, the toggle button for link comparison appears at the baseline compare tab.
   Note: Compare Links: Turn on this option to include links in the comparison. If you do not want links to be considered during the comparison, keep this option Off.
   If the Context Comparison option is not selected, the toggle button does not appear at the baseline compare tab.
   When the toggle button is set to ON, it enables Context Comparison and, when it is set to OFF, the default Global Comparison functionality is applied. If the user has set context comparison for links to "ON", it will retain the selection throughout the session. Once the session expires, the functionality will automatically be set as per the configured admin panel settings.
   Context Based Link Comparison
1. Go to your baseline or create a new one.
2. Now link any two work items from the same baseline as shown in the image below.
3. Link any work item to another work item which is not a part of baseline compare context as shown in the image below.
4. Now, if you switch on the context comparison toggle button, you would see the two work items which were linked together from the same baseline as changed. Whereas, the work item which was linked to a work item outside the baseline shows No Change.
5. If the toggle button is set to OFF, all the work items that experienced a change in the link will be marked as changed irrespective of whether the work item exists in baseline compare context or outside the context.
   Similarly, we can see the work items in baseline compare context as changed while comparing with another baseline.

title: BYOD
answer:
(Admin Panel module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Copilot4DevOps")

The BYOD (Bring Your Own Data) feature in the Copilot4DevOps Admin Panel empowers users to enhance AI-driven outputs by integrating their own data sources, providing a tailored and versatile experience. Offered as a Beta version, this BYOD feature facilitates a customized knowledge base that works alongside global or public data to refine responses, insights, and project management support.
BYOD LICENSING AND ACCESS
There are two distinct BYOD license types available to accommodate varied usage needs:
BYOD with default LLM
BYOD with own LLM
Using ‘BYOD with default LLM’
This option is accessible to users with a basic BYOD license. Those without an active BYOD license will see a red-highlighted message prompting them to activate the license.
• Once activated, the indicator turns green, signaling access to BYOD features.
The BYOD features are accessible now.
Using ‘BYOD with own LLM’
Using ‘BYOD with own LLM’: Users who wish to leverage their own LLM model must secure the "BYOD with BYOLLM" license. When switching to their own LLM, all existing data within the BYOD tab will be removed upon confirmation, ensuring data integrity. Those without an active "BYOD with BYOLLM" license will see a red-highlighted message prompting them to activate the license.
• Once activated, the indicator turns green, signaling access to BYOD features.
The BYOD features are accessible now.
Data Management
The BYOD tab enables users to integrate their own knowledge base, allowing outputs to be generated based on both user-uploaded content and global/public data when the Data Retrieval toggle is enabled. Users can enrich their knowledge base by:
Uploading documents via “Add File”
Adding work items via “Add Query”
Incorporating Wiki pages from Azure DevOps projects via “Add Wiki Pages”
This seamless integration ensures personalized and comprehensive data retrieval to support diverse operational needs.
The behavior of the toggle in each module is as follows:
When the 'Data Retrieval' toggle is On and the checkbox is checked from here (BYOD tab in Admin settings), a 'Use BYOD' toggle will appear next to model selection in each copilot4DevOps function, allowing users to manage data retrieval for that copilot4DevOps function.
If the 'Data Retrieval' toggle is On but the 'Use BYOD' toggle is Off in the copilot4DevOps function, data will not be retrieved from the documents uploaded in BYOD.
If the checkbox is unchecked, the 'Use BYOD' option will not appear next to model selection in any copilot4DevOps function.
ADD FILE
Upload document(s) from anywhere on your device here in this section, you cannot upload image format files, and it should also be practiced that the files uploaded do not contain any images. The files that the user can upload must have the following extensions: no other file types will be accepted, (.c, .cpp, .cs, .css, .csv, .doc, .docx, .go, .html, .java, .js, .json, .md, .pdf, .php, .pptx, .py, .rb, .sh, .tex, .ts, .txt, .xls, .xlsx, .xml).
ADD QUERY
Add work items data by selecting the queries (Only the queries that are part of the shared queries) exists in the Azure DevOps. For retrieval, it will consider the data of each work item including the configured field(s) and details of linked work item(s) if exists within the same query.
ADD WIKI PAGES
Select the Wiki Pages for this section that are available in the Azure DevOps for the selected projects.
Other functionalities in BYOD
Auto Sync for Wiki & Query Data
Copilot4DevOps now supports Auto Sync for Wiki & Query data in the BYOD, allowing users to automatically synchronize their data based on a weekly or monthly schedule.
The Auto Sync Query/Wiki Data is positioned below the Add Wiki section under the BYOD Tab of Admin Panel. The section can be enabled/disabled using the relevant toggle button.
When enabled, users can configure credentials and a sync schedule to keep Wiki and Query data updated automatically.
Key features and behaviors are elaborated below:
1
Auto Sync toggle
Enabled/ON: Configuration fields become editable and active.
Disabled/OFF: Fields are disabled/greyed out, but saved values remain retained
2
Authentication controls
Users must provide: Username & Personal Access Token (PAT)
Validation ensures credentials are required and properly formatted before saving
3
Sync Frequency
Can be done Monthly or Weekly
4
Flexible Scheduling
Sync runs on the user's local time, with the frequency set using the above control
5
Save Scheduler Configuration
A Save Scheduler button appears only when Auto Sync is enabled. Once clicked, the system validates the entered details and saves the schedule, confirming success with a message
Automatic Synchronization Execution
After configuration, synchronization runs automatically at the selected schedule without manual effort, retrieving and storing Azure DevOps Query data and Azure DevOps Wiki data
Status (Last Sync Result)
Displays the most recent sync outcome:
Active, successful [Date]
Expired, Unsuccessful with tooltip (Auto sync unsuccessful: Either due to ADO PAT expired or having no access on work items/wiki in PAT.)
Manual Sync
Manual Sync Functionality: Within the BYOD interface, there is manual sync functionality for Query Data and Wiki Pages, allowing users to sync data on demand. The total upload limit is 100 GB for users operating under the Standard BYOD license.
Delete All
Delete All Functionality: With in the BYOD tab, on the top right, users can find a “Delete All” button. Clicking on the “Delete all” button deletes each and every data uploaded within the BYOD tab such as uploaded files, added queries, and the wiki pages.
• When a user clicks on the “Delete All” button, a deletion warning popup appears in order to make sure the user actually wants to delete the BYOD data that has been uploaded or added. To take the precautionary measure a step ahead, the user will have to write “Delete BYOD” in the text box so that nothing happens by mistake.
• Clicking on the “OK” button will delete all the BYOD data.
Update & Delete Functionality:
• Update: The update functionality is only available in the "ADD File" section. Upon clicking it, the same upload popup will open, and you can update the file in the same way it was uploaded the first time. In the update window, you can only upload the updated version of the same file, no new file can be uploaded.
• Delete: The user can individually delete each uploaded data by clicking on it and then navigating to the “Delete” button in all the three sections. Upon clicking the “Delete” button a confirmation popup will appear to the user to verify the decision.
• Deletion confirmation popup.

Steps:

   Source information includes Source TFS, Source Team Project Collection and the relevant Source Team Project in it.
   2
   The destination project if they want the copied Work Items to be created in a different project on the same Team Foundation Server. They can select either the current project or another project within the same server.
   3
   Area Path: Used to select the desired Area Path (of the target Team Project)
   4
   Iteration Path: Used to select the desired Iteration Path (of the target Team Project)
   5
   Create baseline of copied Work Item(s): If selected then a baseline of the copied Work Items is automatically created in the target Team Project, using the name given in
   6
   Baseline Name: Used to give the desired name to the baseline of target Work Items in case user selects option
   7
   Prefix: The text in the text box is appended before the name of the copying Work Item to be used as the name of the newly copied Work Item.
   8
   Postfix: The text in the text box is appended after the name of the copying Work Item to be used as the name of the newly copied Work Item.
   9
   Parent ID: Used to make destination Work Items as children of the provided Work Item. The Work Item that would become the parent should be from the target Azure DevOps project
   10
   Tag: Used to add tags to the Work Items (that would be created at the destination)
   11
   Link with source work item: If selected then the newly created target Work Items are linked with their source Work Items, respectively.

title: Creating Package Variant
keywords: how do i create package variant
how do i creating package variant
answer:
(Version Packages module, MR 2.0 / NextGen)

Steps:
1. Navigate to the “Variants" tab and click on it.
   The “Variants" tab is now opened.
2. Click on the “New Package Variant” Button.
3. The Create Package Variant pop-up window is now openes. The “General” tab is selected by default.
4. Fill out the fields of the General Tab.
• Navigate to the dropdown menu and select the appropriate "To Project" option. This selection determines the project or team for which the variant package will be created.
• Next, click on the "Open in new tab" icon, denoted by an arrow pointing to a square. This action will open the browsing page of the selected project/team in a new tab. Here, you can view the existing version packages within that project/team.
• Assign a suitable name to the variant package that you are creating. Choose a name that accurately reflects the content or purpose of the package.
• Select the desired folder node under which the variant package will be created.
• Provide a description and tag for the variant package. The description should provide additional information about the package's contents, purpose, or any other relevant details. The tag(s) are labels that help categorize and classify the package. Both the description and tags can be viewed in the "Info" tab.
• Optionally, you can provide a comment for the variant package being created. The comment can be used to add specific notes or instructions related to the package.
5. Click on the Next button to go to "Other options" tab or select the "Other options" tab directly.
6. Follow these steps to configure propagation rules for work items in the variant package being created, using the options available under 'Other Options'.
   Link sub Packages
1. User can link or create the variant of the sub-packages associated with the source version package while creating Version Package variant.
1. Link Sub package(s)
• On selecting, the ‘Sub package(s)’ of the source Version package shall be auto-linked to the Variant package as ‘Sub package’.
2. Create Variant of sub package(s)
• Upon selecting this option, a package variant shall be created of each associated sub-package of a source version package and then shall be auto-linked to the package variant as ‘Sub package’.
• Propagation rules configured on this window shall be applicable between the respective source package and its linked package variant.
3. Don’t link sub package(s)
• On selecting the ‘Sub package(s)’ of the source Version package shall be not be associated with the Variant package as ‘Sub package’.
   Version Package Propagation Rules
• Enable the Version package propagation rules by toggling the corresponding button to the "On" position.
• Check the "A work item is added" checkbox. This ensures that whenever a new work item is added to the source package, it will also be added to the respective target variant package.
• Check the "A work item is removed" checkbox. This ensures that if a work item is removed from the source package, it will also be removed from the corresponding target variant package.
• Check the "A work item is set to locked/live using 'Set Version'" checkbox. This ensures that if a work item is locked to a specific revision or set to live in the source package, the same status will be propagated to the new target package.
8. Click on the “Create” button and the new variant package will be created and opened in Results tab and will be shown in All tab as well as under the Target node in Variants tab.
9. The new variant package has been created.
10. Right click on any version package in the Variants tab to access the Context Menu options
11. Click on Edit Comment and a pop-up will open from where the user will be able to edit the already added comment.
• Make changes to the existing comment.
• Click on the OK button to save the edited comment.
• The edited comment is now reflected in the comment section.
12. Click on the Remove Link option to remove the link between the source and target package. The respective variant package will not be shown in the Variants tab after the link has been removed.
• Click on the "Remove" button
• The respective variant package will not be shown in the Variants tab after the link has been removed.
   Edit Rules From Right Panel
   Select Edit Rules from the right panel. The configured propagation rules for the respective variant package will be shown here and the rules can be edited from there.
   Click on the Save button to save and apply the changes made in the rules.
   Click Cancel to exit the edit rules operation.

Steps:

4. Click on the "Checkout and Enable Editing" button in the yellow bar to switch to edit mode.

7. Choose one of the following options from the 'Save' dropdown:
   Save and Check in
   Saves the document with a minor version increment.
   Save and Check in with Label
   Enter a version label and comments. Choose to save as a major or minor version.
   Download
   Download the document to your device. (Not with the changes, it will download the last saved version)
   Save and Check In

5. The document has been saved with the new version label.
   Download
1. Click on the 'Save' dropdown and select 'Download a Copy' option.
2. The file has been downloaded (the last saved version).
   Version Management
   Version management is a critical aspect of maintaining the integrity and organization of documents. Our established criteria stipulate that minor versions will increment by 0.1, reflecting small changes or updates that do not significantly alter the document's core content.
   Conversely, major versions will increase by 1.0, indicating substantial revisions or significant changes that warrant a new iteration of the document. This structured approach to versioning not only facilitates easy tracking of document progress and revisions but also ensures clarity in communication among team members regarding the nature and extent of changes made.

title: Generating a Diagram
keywords: how do i generating a diagram
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "SOP/Document Generator")

Step 1: Open the Diagram Interface

Steps:
1. Navigate to the Copilot4DevOps main page or open Copilot4DevOps from Queries or Backlogs.
2. Click on the Diagram tile to access the Diagram interface.
   Step 2: Access the "Prompt" Tab
   Upon opening the Diagram interface, you will see two tabs: 'Prompt' and 'Diagram'. By default, the interface opens to the Prompt tab.
   Step 3: Select a Diagram Type
1. In the Prompt tab, click on Select Diagram Type.
   It will open a new window.
2. Choose a diagram type from the window.
   Note: By default, the selection is set to flowchart, which generates diagrams based on the provided prompt or selected Work Item (WI) context or both.
   The following Diagram Types are available for the user to generate a diagram.
• Flowchart
• Sequence Diagram
• Entity Relationship Diagram
• Class Diagram
• State Diagram
• Mindmap
• Journey Diagram
• Context Diagram
   Step 4: Provide Context for the Diagram
   You can generate a diagram by either entering a prompt, selecting a Work Item (WI) for context, or both:
   Option 1: Enter a Prompt
1. In the left panel of the Prompt tab, type a description or instructions for the diagram.
   Example: "Create a flowchart for a CI/CD pipeline."
   A Default prompt for each diagram type will be shown.
• Users can rewrite their prompt using the Rewrite Prompt option in the Diagram function with a single click, producing structured, complete, and accurate prompt—using the AI model selected from the "AI Model Auto Selection and Ranking" section for “Rewrite Prompt” under the General tab in Admin panel.
   Upload File(s)
   The "Upload File(s)" feature has been introduced and is now seamlessly integrated into the Diagram. This capability allows users to attach relevant files that serve as contextual reference material to generate more accurate and tailored diagram outputs.
   Steps to Upload a File
1. Click on the "Upload File(s)" option, found next to the "Rewrite Prompt" button
   A popup window will appear titled Upload File.
   Note: The file/attachment upload process is elaborated in detail here.
   All uploaded files will now be visibly listed below the "Rewrite Prompt" and "Upload File(s)" buttons, clearly indicating the files attached to the current session.
   Note: supported file types, ".xls",".xlsx",".csv",".docx",".xml",".json",".pdf",".txt",".png",".jpg",".webp",".gif",".CSS",".HTML","JS".
   If a file was uploaded by mistake, it can be removed by clicking the "x" (cross) icon next to the file name.
   Option 2: Select a Work Item (WI)
   By Default, the work item from which the Copilot4DevOps feature has been invoked will be shown pre-selected.
1. From the right panel, search for and select a Work Item by ID or title.
2. Select one or multiple work items for context and click on the "OK" button.
   The work item(s) have been added for context.
3. Once selected, you can specify fields from the Work Item to include in the diagram.
   Note: The Fields in the bottom of the right panel will selected by default in accordance to the work item type. However, ID, Title, and Work Item Type are pre-selected fields which cannot be removed.
   Note: Images embedded within the work item's HTML fields (such as Description, Acceptance Criteria, Repro Steps, and Comments) are detected and processed during AI operations. Image references are preserved throughout the operation.
   Step 5: Generate the Diagram
1. Ensure that either a prompt is entered, a Work Item is selected, or both.
   Note: Diagram generation is disabled if no prompt is provided and no Work Item is selected.
2. Click the Generate button.
   Note: Ranked AI model is configured in the Admin Panel for the Diagram, and this will be used for generating the diagram.
   Step 6: View the Diagram
   After generation, the interface will automatically switch to the Diagram tab.
1. Click on the highlighted button, to open the right panel.
2. Interact with the diagram using the available options:
• Zoom In/Out: Adjust the diagram's view.
   To navigate diagrams more easily, you can now use mouse-based controls. Hold Ctrl and scroll the mouse wheel over the diagram to zoom in or out.
   To move around the diagram, click and hold on the canvas, then drag to pan the view, helping you move smoothly without affecting diagram elements.
• Copy Diagram: Copy the diagram to the clipboard.
• Open in a New Window: Open the diagram in a larger view.
   Step 7: Save and Publish the Diagram
   Saving the Diagram
1. After generating or modifying a diagram, click on the Save As option in the interface.
2. Choose the desired format for saving the diagram:
• Word File (.docx): Includes the Diagram, Explanation, and Diagram Markdown.
• PDF File (.pdf): Includes the Diagram, Explanation, and Diagram Markdown.
• Image File (.svg): Saves the Diagram as a standalone image.
   Once the format has been selected the file is downloaded.
3. Click on the downloaded file.
   Users can view the downloaded file.
   Publishing the Diagram
   The user can publish diagrams to Work Items (WIs) either by updating an existing WI or creating a new one:
   Option 1: Publish to an Existing Work Item
1. Choose the option to publish the diagram to Existing Work Item.
   Note: If the diagram was generated using only a prompt and not a work item, the 'Existing Work Item' option will be disabled.
2. Select an existing WI from the provided list and choose the work item field. Only those work items will be shown in this dropdown that have been selected for the context. If no work item has been selected for the context of the diagram user won't be able to publish the diagram to Existing Work Item and the option will be shown disabled.
3. Decide whether to include the explanation and diagram Markdown in the Work Item (WI).
   Note: If the 'Include Explanation' checkbox is not enabled, it indicates that the diagram's explanation has not been generated yet. Should the user click the checkbox, the explanation will be generated in real time. If the explanation has already been generated, the checkbox will be selected by default.
4. Select if you want to replace the selected information in the field and then click on the Publish button.
   The existing work item has been updated successfully.
   Option 2: Publish to a New Work Item
1. Choose the option to create a New Work Item during publishing.
2. A default title for the new WI will be auto-generated. You can edit the title before completing the publishing process.
   Note: The title will include a CpD postfix (e.g., "New Workflow Diagram [CpD]").
3. Select the Work item type.
4. Select the Work item field.
5. Decide whether to include the explanation and diagram Markdown in the new WI.
6. Click on the "Publish" button.
   The new work item with diagram has been published successfully.
   Note: When a work item is created from Copilot4DevOps, it automatically inherits both the Area Path and the Iteration Path of the parent (anchor) work item, keeping child items aligned with their parent's area and sprint and reducing manual effort during planning.
   Before the work item is created, the system validates whether the current user has permission to create or edit work items in the inherited Area Path.
   If the user has access, the work item is created successfully with the inherited Area Path and Iteration Path.
   If the user does not have access to the inherited Area Path, the Work Item window opens so the user can change the Area Path before creating the work item.
   Entering Diagram Markdown to Generate a Diagram
1. If you have a Diagram Markdown you can directly go to the Diagram tab and enter the Diagram Markdown directly to generate a diagram.
2. Directly go to the Diagram tab.
3. Click the Markdown button to open the panel.
4. Paste / Type the Diagram Markdown.
5. The diagram has been generated directly using the Diagram Markdown.
   Rough UI Functionality
   A Rough UI feature enables users to create diagrams with a deliberately hand-drawn, sketch-like aesthetic. This approach is particularly valuable in the early stages of design or ideation, as it prioritizes concept exploration over detailed styling or refined visuals. By simulating the appearance of rough sketches, the feature fosters rapid prototyping and encourages iterative feedback, allowing users to focus on functionality, structure, and user flow rather than visual precision. This informal yet effective presentation style supports collaboration by making it clear that the design is still in a conceptual phase, inviting constructive input and facilitating innovation.

The Copilot4DevOps homepage is designed to help you quickly access, organize, and learn about the features you use most. With personalization options such as favorites, categories, recent activity, and layout customization, you can tailor the homepage to match your workflow.

Customizing the Homepage Layout
