title: Horizontal Matrix using Query method
keywords: trace analysis horizontal matrix using query method
horizontal matrix using query method steps
horizontal matrix using query method procedure
answer:
(Trace Analysis module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Horizontal Matrix")

Steps:
1. Follow Steps in Step 1: Creating a new Traceability Matrix to create the matrix.
2. Once on the Traceability Editor page, select the "Horizontal Matrix" from type of matrix drop down menu.
3. Select the Query from type of matrix drop down menu.
• Options for creating the Horizontal Matrix (using Query) appear on the Editor page.
4. Select the desired Query / Smart Docs / Version Package*.
• When "Only return links that exist in a query" are checked (by default), only work items in query are shown in linked work items. But if unchecked, all linked work items irrespective of the query are shown in linked work items.
   Note: This option is only available if the user has selected any query through Select Query dropdown.
• When "Include sub-package(s)" is unchecked (by default), only work items in source package are displayed in the traceability matrix. But if checked, it includes work item(s) from the tree of sub-package(s) exists in the hierarchy to nth level.
   Note: This option shall only be available if user selected any version package through Select Query dropdown.
5. Select the first Work Item type of the matrix.
6. Click the Add new Work Item link.
7. Similarly select the relevant linked Work Items (if desired).
8. Click the Run Query button after all the linked Work Item types have been selected.
   The Horizontal Matrix is created.
   *Note:
• The matrix would show relations only if these relations show up in the selected Query / Smart Docs / Version Package at the beginning of the process.
• Users should make sure that in the Azure DevOps project queries, the desired Work Items are linked and included in the relevant queries. While in Smart Docs / Version Package, linked work item(s) must be linked with top level/ previous work item according to the link configuration defined in editor tab.
• If the Work Items selected at the later stages of the process are in fact related but do not appear in the selected query / Smart Docs / Version Package (or sub-package(s) hierarchy) then the relevant columns would show up empty.
• If the selected top-level work item is not the root work item in Smart Docs, then the traceability matrix will be generated as empty.
• If the selected top-level work item does not exist in source package, then the traceability matrix will be generated empty.
• If the ‘Include sub-package(s)’ option is checked on editor, then the scenario would be as following:
   If the work item is live or locked in both source and sub-package(s), then the details (hierarchy) would be shown on traceability matrix as it is in version package.
   If the work item has different status on source package and in sub-package (live and locked), then the details (hierarchy) would be shown on traceability matrix only from the source package and would not include details from sub-package.
   If the work item is locked in both source and sub-package(s) but with different revisions, then the details (hierarchy) would be shown on traceability matrix only from the source package and would not include details from sub-package.

New Package
Used to add a new version package as Linked package

Adding a Linked Package From the Right Panel

   New package
   To add linked package, follow these steps:
1. Open the desired Version package.
2. Click the Associated package option from the right panel dropdown.
3. Go to the Linked Packages tab.
4. Select the New package option in the Add dropdown.

   Adding Linked Package From the Work Item Context Menu

   Understanding Permission Options
   Permission
   Functionality / Purpose
   Contribute
   Allows users to upload and make changes to a document.
   Delete
   Allows users to delete the document.
   Manage Permission
   Allows Collection or Project admins to select users or groups who can manage permissions.
   Read:
   Allows users to view, compare, open any version, and view the list of versions. Users cannot edit, download, upload, or check out the files.
   Default Permissions
• By default, only the "Read" permission is set to "Allow (inherited)" for all groups except Project Administrator and Project Collection Administrator.
• For Project Administrator and Project Collection Administrator, all options are set to "Allow."
• For Contributors, the default permission for Contribute is set to "Allow"
   Managing Permissions
• Project Administrators and Project Collection Administrators can change permissions for any group.
• Other groups do not have the ability to change permissions.
   Conflict Resolution
• In scenarios where a user is a member of multiple groups that possess conflicting permissions, it is important to establish a clear hierarchy of authority. In such cases, the "Deny" permission will take precedence over any other permissions granted by the user’s memberships. This prioritization ensures that restrictions are enforced effectively, safeguarding the integrity and security of the system.
   User Notifications
• Users will receive a message if they attempt an action that is denied by their permissions.

   The mapping configuration is applied to all of the headings at this level in the document (for example, all Heading 1 headings in the document).

5. Set the Handling for each detected content section — Paragraphs & Images, List Items & Images, and Tables:
• Ignore — the content is not imported.
• Map to HTML field — the content is added to an HTML field on the work item.
• Create a child work item per paragraph / list — a separate work item is created for each paragraph or list item.
• Each row → work item (Tables only) — each row of the table becomes a work item.
   Topic 2a— Mapping a Table to Work Items
   When a heading contains a table, user can turn each row into a work item and map the table columns to work item fields.
1. In the Tables section, set Handling to Each row → work item.
2. Select the Work item type for the rows created from the table.
3. Optionally, check Ignore header row to exclude the first row from becoming a work item.
4. Under Column → Field mappings, map each extracted column to a work item field (for example, Column 1 → Title).
• Check Ignore this column to exclude a column, or click + Add column to configure additional columns.
5. Use Skip rows · index or range to exclude specific rows (for example, 4 or 1-3, 5). Listed rows will not become work items.
6. To route headings differently based on their text, click Add condition to add an if rule. When a heading contains the specified text, the if mapping applies; otherwise the else mapping is used.
   Note: By default, mapping is set to the ELSE rule, which applies to all headings at this level.
7. Click Next: Map & classify to continue.

title: Publishing a Mockup
keywords: how do i publishing a mockup
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "Mockup")

Publishing the Mockup
Publishing a mock-up is a simple yet critical step in the project workflow. We have discussed this step-by-step here to ensure you do it properly. Follow the steps below to seamlessly publish your mock-up.
You have two options to publish your mockup:

Steps:
1. Publish the Mockup to an Existing Work Item
2. Publish the Mockup to a New Work Item
   Note: Once a work item has been published, it can only be republished to the original work item to which it was first published. During republishing, the "Publish to New Work Item" option will be disabled. Only the "Publish to Existing Work Item" option will be available, with the originally published work item pre-selected and locked to prevent modification by the user.
   However, during the initial publishing process, both options—"Publish to New Work Item" and "Publish to Existing Work Item"—will be enabled, allowing the user to select either.
   To an Existing Work Item
1. Once your mock-up is ready for publishing, the first thing you need to do is click the Publish button. This action triggers the process of publishing your mock-up to a work item.
2. After clicking the Publish button, a menu will appear with options for publishing. Select the Existing Work Item option from this menu to proceed. This will direct you to the next steps for assigning your mock-up to an existing work item.
   A pop-up window will appear titled Publish to Existing Work Item.
   The first mandatory thing you need to do is selecting the Work Item to which you wish to publish your mock-up.
3. Search for the existing work item via ID or Title. Select the Work Item that best aligns with your mock-up.
4. Next, you need to select the Work Item Field where your mock-up will be published. Choose a field that best fits the type of content you are attaching.
   The Link to workitem field is preselected with the workitem you choose as a reference.
5. Now the user has to select the link type for the Link type drop down menu.
   Mandatory Fields Scenario
• Mandatory fields for a work item appear within a light gray box labeled Mandatory Fields.
   Note: Mandatory fields only appear when the user configures specific fields as mandatory. If no mandatory fields are configured, the mandatory fields option does not display. When mandatory fields are configured and the user does not provide values for them, the 'Publish' button remains disabled until the user enters the mandatory information. If no mandatory fields are configured by the user, the button remains enabled by default.
• Mandatory fields for a work item appear within a light gray box labeled Mandatory Fields.
• A red icon marks required fields, clearly showing that they must be filled in.
• Add the required field info in the fields mentioned in the ‘Mandatory Field' box.
• Once you enter information in the field, the red label beside it is removed.
• The Publish button becomes enabled only after you complete all required fields for the work item type selected in the Create Work Item window.
   Below the Link Type selection, you'll see a Check Box labeled Add Mock-Up File(s) in Attachment.
6. If you want your mockup files to be attached, check the box to enable the attachment functionality.
   Note: When the work item has been updated, the added attachments will be visible in ADO.
   At the bottom of the pop-up window, there will be another check box labeled "Replace selected information in the field". This option allows you to replace the existing information in the chosen field with your new mock-up.
7. If you want to update the field with the new mock-up, check this box. If you do not wish to replace the existing content, leave the box unchecked.
8. Once you have completed all the necessary fields and options, review your selections carefully. When you are satisfied with your inputs click the Publish button. This will push your mock-up to the selected work item and field, updating it accordingly.
9. Once done, the updated work item can be seen by the user below the prompt area along with a notification that the Work Item # updated successfully.
   The updated Work Item now contains the mockup details in the selected field of the Work Item.
10. Along with the updated existing work item that is shown below, you will see a Copilot4DevOps icon. With this option you can open the work item in any other feature of Copilot4DevOps.
   To a New Work Item
1. Start by clicking the Publish button. This will open the options for publishing your mock-up.
2. Out of the two options, select the New Work Item option to proceed with creating a new work item and publishing the mock-up.
   A pop-up window will appear with several mandatory fields to complete.
3. The first field you'll need to fill in is the Work Item Title. This is where you define the title of the new work item. Enter a unique title for the new work item that clearly describes its purpose.
4. Choose the appropriate Work Item Type.
   This field will allow you to categorize the new work item.
5. Next, you will need to select the Work Item Field where your mock-up will be published. Choose the field in which the mock-up's details will be stored.
6. If you want the mockup file to be attached to the Work Item, enable the Add MockUp File(s) in Attachments check box.
   Note: When the new work item has been created, the added attachments will be visible in ADO.
7. After filling out the necessary fields and making your selections, Click Publish.
   The Work Item is created along with a notification at the top, and a link to the newly created Work Item at the bottom.
   Note: When a work item is created from Copilot4DevOps Chat, it automatically inherits both the Area Path and the Iteration Path of the parent (anchor) work item, keeping child items aligned with their parent's area and sprint.
   Before the work item is created, the system validates whether the current user has permission to create or edit work items in the inherited Area Path.
   If the user has access, the work item is created successfully with the inherited Area Path and Iteration Path.
   If the user does not have access to the inherited Area Path, the Chat responds inline, informing the user that they do not have permission to create the work item in the inherited Area Path and prompting them, within the chat, for how they want to proceed.
8. Clicking the link opens the Work Item in ADO.
   Along with the New Work Item you will see a Copilot4DevOps icon. With this option you can open the new work item in any other feature of Copilot4DevOps.

title: Reuse Work Items
answer:
(Baseline module, MR 2.0 / NextGen)

• Reuse Work Items work the same way as Copy Work items, but for a different purpose.
• In Copy Work Items, users copy Work Items from the current Team Project to another Team Project
• In Reuse Work Items, users fetch Work Items from another Team Project and bring them into the current Team Project.
• In reality new Work Items are created in both copy and reuse but with all the properties of the source Work Items.
• The source Team Project can also be the target Team Project. i.e. Users have the option to reuse Work Items from the same Team Project or another Team Project.
The process to reuse Work Items is elaborated in the following steps:

Steps:
1. Open the target Team Project in which the Work Items are to be reused.
2. Click on the Reuse Button on the Browse Page.
3. Set the Source TFS information and then click the Input Type option in the window.
4. Finalize the Option settings and click the Next Button.
4. Select the relevant baseline.
5. Select the desired Work Items and click the Reuse Button.
   The baseline of the selected Work Item is created
   The newly created baseline is automatically opened.

title: Shared Chats
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "Chat")

Copilot4DevOps now supports viewing and continuing conversations in Shared Chats, enabling team members to collaborate on the same chat thread while ensuring only one user can actively use a shared chat at a time through a locking mechanism.
Previously Shared Chats used to be read-only, however, team members can now open Shared Chats and continue the conversation.
Shared chats remain visible for all users, while active usage is controlled through single-user locking.
Key features & behavior
Team-Wide Shared Chat Access
All users in the team can see and open chats available under Shared Chats.
Any team member can send messages and extend the chat thread when the chat is not locked.
Single-User Locking
The first user to send a prompt becomes the active user and the chat is locked for others.
If another user is active, the chat appears disabled and users see the message: “This chat is currently being used by {UserName}. You can continue after it is closed. Please Refresh to check the status.”
A Refresh button allows users to check the latest status and regain access once the lock is released.
Lock Release Conditions
Lock is released automatically when:
The active user closes the chat
The active user navigates away (switches tab/chat)
The session is idle for 10 minutes
Move to My Chat option
If the initiating user selects Move to My Chats, the chat is moved back to their My Chats. But, this will only happen if no one has continued the conversation in the Shared Chat. If any user has continued the chat in the shared space, then the chat cannot be moved back.
To prevent conflicts, shared chats cannot be moved or deleted while multiple users are engaged, ensuring safe collaboration and consistent chat ownership.

title: SOP/Document Generator
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help)

The SOP / Document Generator is specifically designed to create relevant SOPs & Documents for the corresponding Work Items.

Steps:
1. To begin, navigate to the Backlog or Queries section where all work items are listed. Browse through the list and identify the work item for which you want to generate an SOP / Document. This will serve as a reference for the SOP Document you are about to create.
2. Click on the ellipsis button and then select the Copilot4DevOps option.
   The Copilot4DevOps window opens.
3. On the Home Page, you will find the SOP / Document Generator option. Click on this option to open the corresponding tool.
   The SOP / Document Generator window will appear. This window contains essential functionalities for generating a document.
   At the top left corner, you will see two main tabs: the Prompt Tab and the Result Tab.
   The Prompt Tab helps with structuring the document
   The Result Tab displays the final output based on inputs provided.
4. Other functions can be accessed that are a part of Copilot4DevOps pop-up from this breadcrumb dropdown.
5. When you click on the help icon showing with the breadcrumb, the right panel will open, displaying the help content related to the currently open function.
6. When the SOP / Document Generator window opens, the Prompt Tab is selected by default. This tab serves as the main input area for instructions that guide the document creation process.
   Below the tabs, there is an option labeled Document Type/Title.
   a. By default, the title setting is set to Auto. With this setting enabled, the system will automatically generate a title for the SOP/Document based on the document’s content and work item details.
   b. If you prefer, you can manually enter a title for the document. Simply type in your desired title in the provided text field.
   The window layout consists of two panels:
1. Left Panel
2. Right Panel
   Left Panel
   The Left Panel is where you provide instructions for generating the document. Here, you need to enter a structured prompt that defines the key elements of your document.
   a. To ensure a well-structured document, enter clear and detailed instructions in the Left Panel. These instructions should outline the key components the SOP document should include. The more detailed and specific your input, the more accurate and useful the generated document will be.
7. If you find that your initial prompt instructions are unclear or ineffective, you can refine them using the Rewrite Prompt option located at the bottom of the Left Panel. This allows you to adjust and improve your instructions before proceeding with document generation.
   Note: Using the AI model selected from the "AI Model Auto Selection and Ranking" section for “Rewrite Prompt” under the General tab in Admin panel.
   The prompt is rewritten.
   Upload File(s)
   The "Upload File(s)" feature allows users to attach relevant files that serve as contextual reference material to generate more accurate and tailored SOP/Document Generator outputs.
   The "Upload File(s)" button is located next to the "Rewrite Prompt" button within the Copilot – SOP/Document Generator interface.
   Steps to Upload a File
11. Click on the "Upload File(s)" button, found next to the "Rewrite Prompt" button
   A popup window will appear titled Upload File.
   Note: The file/attachment upload process is elaborated in detail here.
   All uploaded files will now be visibly listed below the "Rewrite Prompt" and "Upload File(s)" buttons, clearly indicating the files attached to the current session.
   Note: supported file types, ".xls",".xlsx",".csv",".docx",".xml",".json",".pdf",".txt",".png",".jpg",".webp",".gif",".CSS","."JS".
   If a file was uploaded by mistake, it can be removed by clicking the "x" (cross) icon next to the file name.
   Right Panel
   Additionally, you can enhance your SOP document by referencing existing work items, By default, the work item(s) that you selected when opening the Copilot window will be selected here.
   a) Select one or more work items to provide additional context. This ensures that the generated SOP Document aligns with specific tasks and requirements within your workflow.
• An "Add Work Item(s)" pop up window will now open with the option of adding work items using Query or Work Item(s).
• Add the work items that you want to use as a reference for your document.
   b) Make sure the toggle button for “Pass Work Item(s) as reference” is ON if you want to use the selected work items as a reference for document generation.
12. The Fields section allows you to specify attributes of the selected work items that should be included in the SOP document.
   By default, the following fields are pre-selected:
• ID
• Title
• Work Item Type
   However, you have the flexibility to select additional fields as needed to provide more context and relevant details in the SOP / Document.
   Note: Images embedded within the work item's HTML fields (such as Description, Acceptance Criteria, Repro Steps, and Comments) are detected and processed during AI operations. Image references are preserved throughout the operation.
   Other Options
13. If you have pre-written prompts or instructions, you can insert them directly into the Prompt Area using the Insert Text Block option. This feature enables you to seamlessly add existing content, eliminating the need to manually retype information.
14. Ranked AI models configured in the Admin Panel will be displayed for each corresponding feature on the Home Page.
15. The Use BYOD (Bring Your Own Data) toggle button allows you to generate documents based on the uploaded data. When enabled, the system will use data stored in the Admin Section to create the SOP/Document. If you want the system to reference existing data sources, make sure to activate this toggle before generating the document.
   Note: If BYOD is enabled, the recommended BYOD model will be set; otherwise, the non-BYOD model will remain as the recommended one.
   .
   When Use BYOD is enabled, images embedded within BYOD-enabled documents are also extracted and processed, and are available as input to the AI model along with their associated text.
16. For further customization, use the Custom Instructions option. Click on Custom Instructions option at top right of the breadcrumb, a right panel opens.
   From the right panel you can see the AI Service selected in the Admin Panel. You are also able to Choose Type of Conversation Style such as “More Creative”, “More Balanced” or “More Precise”. Furthermore, you also have the option to specify the Response Language and even choose the output length such as “Long”, “Medium” or “Short”
   By adjusting these settings, you can ensure that the SOP/Document adheres to your organization’s communication standards and preferred writing style.
   Generate
18. Before generating the document, ensure that all settings—including prompts, model selection, fields, and additional configuration are properly set. This step is crucial to obtaining an accurate and comprehensive document.
19. Once the mandatory input, i.e Prompt, is given, the Generate button will become enabled.
   This button is divided into two options: Generate and Generate with Q&A.
   Generate with Q&A
   Click Generate button and then select the Generate with Q&A option.
   a. If you select Generate with Q&A, a pop-up window will appear, automatically generating 10 questions based on the given prompt / instructions.
   Note: The questions generated are derived from the instructions provided in the Prompt Tab. These questions help ensure that the document covers essential details. Review the questions listed in the pop-up window and select the ones you wish to include in the final SOP document.
   b. Select the desired questions.
   c. By default, the system provides pre-selected answers for generated questions. However, you can manually edit these answers before finalizing the document. This ensures that the responses align with specific operational guidelines and requirements.
   d. In case you need more than 10 questions, the See more feature within the Q&A pop-up allows you to create additional questions beyond the default limit. Use this option to expand the depth of the Q&A section as needed.
   e. Click on the Generate button within the pop-up window. This will incorporate the selected Q&A section into the SOP document, enhancing its comprehensiveness and clarity.
   Note: The system will automatically switch to the Results tab to display the generated document.
   Generate
   a. If you prefer not to include a Q&A section, simply click on the Generate button without selecting the Q&A option.
   b. This will produce a standard SOP document based on your configurations without additional question-and-answer content.
   Note: The system will automatically switch to the Results tab to display the generated document.
20. When document generation is complete, two options appear at the bottom of the results screen:
1. Regenerate
2. Save
1. Regenerate
• If you want to make changes to the document, use the Regenerate button to generate a revised version.
• At the bottom of the results page, a Text Area displays the instructions or prompt used for document generation. If necessary, update the content in this text area and click Regenerate to create a new version of the SOP document.
2. Save
• To save the document, click on the Save As button.
• You will then see two format options: Save as Word or Save as PDF. Choose the preferred format and proceed with saving the document to your system.
   Note: You can select only files with the following extensions: .doc, .docx, .dotx, .docm, .dotm
• When you click on either Save as MS Word or Save as PDF, a popup will appear.
1. In the popup, click Select files... if you want to upload your own template.
2. Below that, you will see a Template drop down with two categories:
• Default (Example templates have been shared by us for your guidance)
• Uploaded Templates (user-defined, uploaded via “Select files...”)
   Note: Default.docx template is available by default. Uploaded Templates will only show if you have added custom templates.
3. Select your preferred template from the drop down and then click OK button.
4. The system will generate the document based on the selected template and automatically download it to your system.
5. Duplicate File Name Handling
• If you try to upload a template with the same name as an already existing one, a popup will display: "This file name already exists."
   Note: You will need to rename your file before uploading again or delete the previous one.
6. You can delete any uploaded template if it’s no longer needed:
• Next to each template, you will see a ❌ (cross) icon.
7. Upon clicking the cross icon, a confirmation box will appear:
• Yes → Template will be permanently deleted.
• No → Action will be cancelled, and the window will close.
21. If the generated document includes images, you can:
• Open the diagram in a new tab by clicking this button.
• Or interact with them by clicking an image to view it in a pop-up.
• Zoom in or out for better visibility.
• Download it separately. Available download formats include .SVG, and .HTML.
22. If the generated document includes a mockup, you can view it directly within the document or open it in a new tab by clicking this button.

title: Status of Versions
answer:
(Smart Docs module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Version Management")

Status of Versions in Version Management (Smart Docs)
• The ‘Approved’, ‘Rejected’, ‘Incomplete’, ‘Reviewed’ and ‘Complete’ status is shown only for review version(s) of closed review(s) in version management window and when these versions are opened. For other review(s) that are not closed yet, ‘Active’ status is shown for their version(s) and for Smart Docs versions, ‘N/A’ is shown in only version management window.
• Cancel Review: Whenever a review is initiated and then canceled through "Cancel Review" option in “Review” module having either reviewers or approvers or both then for such review "Cancelled" status is shown in "Version Management" pop-up and respective "Opened Review Version" of the cancelled review in Smart Docs module.
• When there are only approvers or both reviewers and approvers in a closed review and all approvers have approved all work items and all reviewers have reviewed (submit review) as well then for such review "Approved" status is shown.
• When there are both "Approvers" and "Reviewers" in a review and approvers have approved all work item(s) and some reviewers have reviewed (submit review) some work item(s) whereas "Review Completed" is performed on rest of the work item(s) or if "Review Completed" is performed on all work item(s) by the reviewer and then the review was closed then for such review “Approved” status is shown.
• When there are only approvers or both approvers and reviewers in a closed review and an approver "Rejects" a work item and reviewers have reviewed (submit review) as well or performed review completed or any other action then for such review “Rejected” status is shown.
• When there are both reviewers and approvers in a closed review and all approvers have provided their responses (approved) on all work items but not all reviewers have provided their responses (submit review) on all work items or if all reviewers have provided responses on some work items and not on all work items and "vice versa" as well then for such review “Incomplete” status is shown.
• When there are both reviewers and approvers in a closed review and reviewers have done "Submit Review" on some work items and "Review Completed" on other work items or if "Review Completed" is performed on all work items by the reviewer(s) and if an approver has approved some work item(s) and not all work item(s) or if some approvers have provided their feedback on some work item(s) and not on all work item(s) well then for such review “Incomplete” status is shown.
• The ‘Reviewed’ status shows when there are only reviewers in a closed review and all of the reviewers have reviewed (submit review) all work items.
• When there are only reviewers in a review and some reviewers have reviewed (submit review) some work item(s) and "Review Completed" is performed on the rest of the work item(s) or if reviewers perform “Review Completed” on all work item(s) and then the review was closed then for such review “Complete” status is shown.
• Whenever a review is initiated and then canceled through "Cancel Review" option in “Review” module having either reviewers or approvers or both then for such review "Cancelled" status is shown.
   Note: The status shown in Smart Docs module for closed review version(s) is similar to that shown in Review module for their respective review(s).

title: Sub Diagrams
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "SOP/Document Generator")

Accessing Sub Diagrams
Users can decompose complex diagrams into Sub Diagrams for better clarity and management. A Sub Diagram tab lists all sub diagrams originating from the main diagram.

Steps:
1. Click on the Sub Diagram Icon in the right-side panel.
   A Sub Diagram tab will appear in the interface.
   Note: You cannot proceed to Sub Diagrams until the associated Work Item (WI) is published.
2. To publish the WI, follow the publishing workflow in Diagram.
3. Once the WI is published, access and interact with the Sub Diagrams as needed. Click on your required Sub-diagram.
   The selected Sub Diagram is generated .
   Publishing Sub Diagrams
   Just like regular Diagrams, users can also publish Sub Diagrams to Existing Work Items and New Work Items. Let's discuss each of the two ways.
   To an Existing Work Item
1. Click on the "Publish" button.
2. Select the Existing Work Item option.
   Users must publish work items at each level of the diagram hierarchy before generating further sub-diagrams.
   The following pop up window will open.
3. Select the Link Type from the dropdown (By default, Child will be selected as the Link type).
4. Select the work item from the list.
   Note: All Work Items (WIs) will be shown in the list except those that already contain a diagram.
5. Select the Work item field for the sub-diagram.
6. Choose whether you want to include Diagram Explanation.
   Note: In cases where a diagram explanation has not been pre-generated, the checkbox will be displayed as unchecked by default. If the user chooses to check this box, the system will initiate the generation of the explanation in real-time. Conversely, if the checkbox is already checked upon first interaction, it indicates that the explanation has been pre-generated and is readily available.
7. Determine whether to select the "Include Diagram Markdown" option (the option is selected by default).
8. Decide whether to replace the information in the selected field.
9. Click on the "Publish" button.
   The sub-diagram has been published to an existing work item.
   Note: When a sub-diagram is successfully published, a green checkbox will appear with its name, serving as an indicator of its published status. For sub-diagrams that are not yet published, a blue plus sign (+) will be displayed adjacent to their names within the sub-diagram panel, signifying their unpublished status and availability for further action.
   To a New work Item
1. To publish a Sub Diagram to a new work item, click on the Publish button.
2. Select the New Work Item option to open the "Publish to new work item" popup window.
3. Select the Link Type. By default "Child" will be selected as the link type.
4. By default, the title of a new work item is automatically set to the name of the diagram. However, users have the flexibility to modify the title as needed to better align with their specific requirements.
5. Select the Work item type.
6. Select the Work item Field.
7. Select whether you wish to include the Explanation and Diagram Markdown in the new work item.
8. Click on the Publish button.
   The Sub Diagram has been successfully published to a New Work item.
   Note: A notification message is triggered above the Sub Diagram list when there is a change or update in the diagram. This can happen in the following scenarios:
• If any changes are made to the diagram using the Diagram Markdown or the Update Diagram prompt.
• The message will notify users that the diagram has been updated and suggests regenerating Sub Diagrams.
   Saving a Sub Diagram
1. To save a sub diagram, the first step is to click on the Save As button.
2. Choose the desired format for saving the sub diagram:
• Word File (.docx): Includes the Diagram, Explanation, and Diagram Markdown.
• PDF File (.pdf): Includes the Diagram, Explanation, and Diagram Markdown.
• Image File (.png/.jpeg): Saves the Diagram as a standalone image.
   The Sub Diagram has been downloaded successfully.
   Accessing Sub Diagrams in a Previous Version of a Diagram
   If you want to view the sub-diagrams for a previous version, please restore it to the latest version and then regenerate the sub-diagrams.
   Note: When you switch to a previous version of the diagram, the Sub Diagrams panel will be frozen and the user will see a message indicating the user to restore the version in order to view the sub diagrams.

title: Sub Package
answer:
(Version Packages module, MR 2.0 / NextGen — under "Smart Edit in the Right panel")

Sub Package in Version Packages
• Sub-packages are smaller packages contained within a larger package, used to organize, and manage related components or features within a larger package.
• Following are the Sub packages options:
Existing Package
Used to add any existing version package as a sub package
New Package
Used to add a new version package as sub package
Edit Comment
Used to edit the linked comment
Remove Link
Used to remove the version package as a sub package
• Users can add sub package from the right panel or from work item context menu options.
Adding Sub Package From The Right Panel
Users can add either a new or any existing version package as sub package.
Existing version package
To add sub package, follow the below steps:

Steps:
1. Open the desired Version package.
2. Click the Associated package option from the right panel dropdown.
3. Go to the ‘Sub Packages’ tab.
4. Select the Existing package option in the Add dropdown.
5. Select the Project, Version Package, and add a link comment on the ‘Add existing package’ popup.
6. Click on the “OK” button.
7. The package will be shown in the right panel under the ‘Sub Packages’ tab along with an indicator in the right panel. Hovering over the indicator shows the count of sub packages the current version package is associated.
   New package
   To add sub package, follow these steps:
1. Open the desired Version package.
2. Click the Associated package option from the right panel dropdown.
3. Go to the ‘Sub Packages’ tab.
4. Select the New package option in the Add dropdown.
5. Add Name, Description, Tag, and link comment, and select the folder, and package template on the General tab of the ‘New package’ popup.
6. Add work items from the ‘Work items’ tab on the New package popup (if any)
7. Click on the ‘Create’ button.
8. The new package will be shown in the right panel under the ‘Sub Packages’ tab along with an indicator in the right panel. Hovering over the indicator shows the count of sub packages the current version package is associated.
   Adding Sub Package From The Work Item Context Menu
   The guidelines to add sub package from work item context menu are discussed here:
1. Open the desired Version package.
2. Select work item(s) and open context menu options.
3. Select “New sub package” option.
4. Add Name, Description, Tag, and link comment, and select the folder, and package template on the General tab of the ‘New package’ popup.
5. Add work items from the ‘Work items’ tab on the New package popup (if any)
6. Click on the ‘Create’ button.
7. The package will be shown in the right panel under the ‘Sub Packages’ tab along with an indicator in the right panel. Hovering over the indicator shows the count of sub packages the current version package is associated..
8. If a work item is associated with one or more sub package(s), an indicator will be shown in the Status column of the Version Package grid.
9. All the version package(s) where the current version package is added as a sub package is shown under <Opened version package name> is included as a sub-package in label.

smart docs template designer ui procedure

title: Test Case Management
answer:
(MR 2.0 / NextGen)

Test Case Management in Modern Requirements4DevOps
In Azure DevOps, the default testing hierarchy supports basic test management. However, for organizations requiring a more comprehensive test management solution, Modern Requirements4DevOps provides an enhanced environment tailored to meet these needs. The following provides an overview of how Modern Requirements4DevOps enables advanced test case management, including features like virtual work items and Smart Reports.
Testing Hierarchy Supported By Azure DevOps
Advanced Test Case Management Offered by Modern Requirements4DevOps
Virtual Work Items
Modern Requirements4DevOps addresses the gap between traditional testing strategies and the limitations of Azure DevOps by offering Virtual Work Items.
These virtual work items can be utilized in the following modules:
• Smart Report (within the Queries tab, Test Hub, and Smart Docs)
• Trace Analysis (in Horizontal Matrix - Test Reporting)
Key Features:
Traceability: Virtual work items are used to create Horizontal Matrices in the Traceability module, linking to existing work items via Virtual Links.
• These virtual Work Items are linked with existing work Items using Virtual Link.
Customization: Virtual properties can be added to each virtual work item through column options.
Smart Report Integration: Virtual links are available under Smart Docs, Queries, and the Test Hub.
Hierarchical Structure: The following hierarchy can be created in both Smart Reports and the Traceability module:
Test Plan vs Test Suite vs Test Case/Test Point vs Test Run vs Test Result vs Test Step Run vs Bugs
Test Case coverage from Test Hub using Smart Report
An essential feature for managing Test Case coverage within the application is the availability of the Smart Report under the Test Plan. This functionality can be accessed via the context menu of the relevant Test Suite, providing users with a streamlined approach to generating detailed, organized reports for test coverage analysis.
Steps to Create Test Plan

Steps:
1. Click Test Plans in the left-side panel.
2. Select Test Plans from the dropdown list.
3. Click New Test Plan and enter the necessary details, then click Create.
   The Test Plan is created.
   The next step is to create Test suites.
   Steps to Create Test Suites
1. Once the Test Plan has been created, hover over the Test Plan name and click the More''option.
2. Go to New Suite → Requirement-Based Suite.
   To create Requirements based suite, we need to add requirements category Work Items.
3. Ensure that Microsoft.RequirementCategory Work Item Type is selected.. Then click the Run query option.
4. Select the desired Work Items and click the Create Suites option.
   The Test suites are created. Now we need to add relevant Test Cases to these suites. For this purpose new as well as existing Test Case Work Items can be used.
   Add Test Cases to Test Suites
1. Choose the appropriate option to add new or existing Test Case Work Items.
2. Select Microsoft.TestCaseCategory Work Item Type and click on the Run query option.
3. Select the desired work items and click on the "Add Test Cases" button.
   Selected Test Case Work Items have been added.
   Generating Smart Reports
1. To generate a Smart Report, click on the three dots at the end of the relevant Test Suite and select Smart Report.
2. In Smart Report, design the report by choosing the required hierarchy (as described above). The exact steps to design a Smart Report can be referred to under the Smart Report section.
3. After the Smart Report is designed as per Test Case requirements the output can be generated. Two options are available for report generation:
• Generate Report: Generates a report for the selected suite.
• Generate Report Including Suites Hierarchy: Generates a report for the selected suite along with its associated test suites in the hierarchy.
   Before clicking on the Generate Report or Generate Report including Suites Hierarchy option, at this point, Users can also filter Test Report data based on selected configurations. Refer to the Customizing the Report section below.
   Customizing the Report
1. To optimize the data shown, select the Settings icon (located at the top right) in the Smart Report.
   A pop-up displays all project configurations; by default, all configurations are selected.
2. Choose specific configurations as per your requirement.
3. Select the desired Report Parts and Style Sheet from the available options.
   Note: This configuration option is applicable only to Smart Parts containing Test Point virtual work items.
4. Click on “Generate” or “Generate Report including Suites hierarchy” to produce the report with the selected configuration filters.
   Generating Report using the "Generate" Report option
1. Click on the Generate button.
2. The Test Report is generated with the data based on the selected configurations only.
   Generating Report using the "Generate Report including Suites hierarchy " Option
1. Clicking Generate Report including Suites hierarchy opens a pop-up named Include Test Suites hierarchy.
2. In this pop-up, multiple test suites can be selected and they are presented in a hierarchical format with associated checkboxes, following the hierarchy present in the Test Hub.
   Note: Using this option allows us to generate a Smart Report for the selected test suite along with its associated test suites in the hierarchy from the test hub.
• The hierarchy is automatically selected for the first 25 suites by default. This count can be modified according to the web configuration settings.
   Note: To generate the Smart Report at least one test suite must be selected. A Maximum of 25 test suites can be chosen by marking the checkboxes. Upon reaching this limit and attempting to select a 26th test suit, a message will be displayed indicating that the “Test suite limit exceeds”.
• When a single test suite is selected, all the test runs are shown.
3. The report can be generated by clicking Generate button on the popup.
   The Smart Report is generated including Suites hierarchy.
   Test Case coverage from Queries using Smart Report
• For test case coverage from Queries using smart report, go to the queries tab in the left panel.
• Select the work items created from the Test Hub using 'My Queries'
• For test case coverage from Queries using smart report, go to the queries tab in the left panel.
• Select the work items created from the Test Hub using 'My Queries'
• To generate a test case API, you need to have the following as your work items.
• Test Plan
• Test Suite
• Test Case
• Click on "Smart Report" in the drop down menu.
   Test Case coverage from Smart Docs using Smart Report
• For test case coverage from Smart docs, go to the smart docs hub from the left panel
• Create a new document in Smart Docs by first adding a root work item, followed by any desired hierarchy such as a section work item, requirement work item, or any other relevant work item. Users can then link test artifacts (Test Plans, Test Suites, and Test Cases) to these items. Once linked, comprehensive Test API reports can be generated directly from Smart Docs, ensuring complete testing traceability, reducing manual effort, and improving documentation efficiency. (How to create a new smart document)
• Now, click on the 'insert work item option from the tool bar.
• In the panel on the right (as shown in the image below) insert the work items that you created from the Test Hub
• After adding test plan, test suite and test case as work items, click on the 'Smart Report' button in the smart docs tool bar.
   Note: While using Smart Report in Smart Docs, the default section should have work item type “Any” or root work item type.
   Filter-based Search for Test Run
• To optimize data retrieval and reduce processing time, users can employ filters in both the Trace Analysis and Smart Report modules (Test Hub, Smart Docs, and Queries Tab).

title: Text Block Management
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help)

The Text Block Management feature in the Copilot4DevOps module allows users to manage and reuse predefined text blocks effectively. This feature enhances productivity by providing an intuitive interface for adding, editing, deleting, and searching text blocks. Users can utilize these text blocks in custom instructions, dynamic prompts, impact analysis, and more.
   Note: This feature is available only to users with a Plus / Ultimate license. Confirm your account license by checking your subscription details in the account settings. Upgrade to a Plus or Ultimate license if necessary.
Accessing Text Block Management From the Copilot4DevOps Homepage

Steps:
1. Go to the main Copilot4DevOps homepage.
2. Look at the top right corner of the homepage. Locate and click on the Text Block Management option, positioned before the News/Tips section.
3. A pop-up window will appear, divided into three tabs: "My Text Blocks", "Shared Text Blocks", "System Text Blocks"
   Accessing Text Block Management From Any Copilot4DevOps Feature
1. Open any Copilot4DevOps feature.
2. Click on the Text Block Management option on the top right.
3. The Text Block Management window now opens.
   However, there are a few differences in this feature-based accessibility.
• Tag-Based Filtering: When a feature is accessed and its name matches any of the tags associated with the stored text blocks, the system will filter and display only those text blocks that contain the corresponding tag. This ensures that users can quickly find relevant text blocks based on specific features.
   Note: If the user wants to see all the available Text Blocks they can do so by removing the tag filter.
   Fallback Display: If the tag corresponding to the feature name is not found in any text block, the system will display all available text blocks, allowing the user to browse through the entire set of stored text for potential matches.
   Automatic Tagging: When creating a new text block from within any feature, the system will automatically generate a tag based on the name of the feature. This ensures that the newly created text block is properly categorized and easily retrievable later.
   These features enhance the organization and efficiency of managing text blocks, making it easier for users to work with relevant content while minimizing manual effort.
   My Text Blocks
   The My Text Block tab is a personalized section within the Text Block Management interface, designed to allow users to manage their own collection of text blocks. Upon logging in, users are presented with a list of their personal text blocks, which they can add, update, or delete as needed.
   The Prefix in Name for My Text Blocks starts with a single backslash(\)
   Shared Text Blocks
   Shared Text Blocks are a type of text block that can be accessed and used by multiple users within the system. These text blocks are typically created by one user but shared with others, allowing them to view, use, and update the text blocks as needed. The key purpose of Shared Text Blocks is to enable collaboration and standardization across teams or users.
   The Prefix in Name for Shared Text Blocks starts with a double backslash(\\)
   Here are the key points about Shared Text Blocks:
• Collaboration: Multiple users can reuse the same predefined text blocks, ensuring consistency across different workflows, projects, or teams.
• Re-usability: Users can access shared text blocks for reuse in their own tasks, improving productivity by leveraging previously created content.
• Visibility: Shared text blocks are available to anyone with a valid Plus or Ultimate license. Users can see both their own shared text blocks and those shared by others.
   System Text Blocks
   System Text Blocks are a centralized repository designed to store and manage text blocks that can be shared across all users. These text blocks are read-only, meaning users can view and use them but cannot modify them. They serve as reusable elements that can be inserted into custom instructions or prompt areas. The primary feature of System Text Blocks is that they can only be cloned, not edited, and cloned text blocks can be stored in either the "My Text Block" or "Shared Text Block" sections.
   The Prefix in Name for System Text Blocks starts with a triple backslash(\\\)

title: Understanding Mockup UI
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "Mockup")

When a user open the Mockup feature in Copilot4DevOps, the interface displays two main tabs and a History Panel to access previously generated diagrams while the user is on any of the tabs:

Steps:
1. Prompt Tab: The Prompt tab is where you set up your inputs and references before generating a mockup.
2. Result Tab: The Result tab shows the mockup that is generated based on your input.
   Prompt Tab
   By default, the Prompt tab is active when you launch the feature.
   This tab is divided into two panels:
   Left panel – your Prompt Area
   Right panel – your Work Item Reference area
   Using the Left Panel (Prompt Area)
   The left panel is where you craft and refine your prompt.
1. Enter your detailed instructions for the mockup you want to generate. Be clear and descriptive about what you expect.
   Rewrite a Prompt
   Rewrite Prompt generates a detailed, well-structured version of your input prompt. It expands and refines your instructions to create a clear specification that helps produce accurate and high-quality mockups.
2. If you want to improve the effectiveness of your existing prompt and get better results, click Rewrite Prompt.
   The system will automatically rewrite your prompt to make it more precise, comprehensive, and outcome-focused.
   Upload a File
   The "Upload File(s)" feature allows users to attach relevant files that serve as contextual reference material to generate more accurate and tailored Mockup outputs.
   Steps to Upload a File
3. Click on the "Upload File(s)" option, found next to the "Rewrite Prompt" button
   A popup window will appear titled Upload File.
   Note: The file/attachment upload process is elaborated in detail here.
   All uploaded files will now be visibly listed below the "Rewrite Prompt" and "Upload File(s)" buttons, clearly indicating the files attached to the current session.
   Note: supported file types, ".xls",".xlsx",".csv",".docx",".xml",".json",".pdf",".txt",".png",".jpg",".webp",".gif",".CSS",".HTML""JS".
4. If a file was uploaded by mistake, it can be removed by clicking the "X" (cross) icon next to the file name.
   Using the Right Panel (Work Item Reference)
   The Right Panel is where you select the work items that you want to use as references for the mockup.
   By default, the work item you initially selected to open the Mockup feature is pre-selected here.
   You can also select multiple work items as references by clicking the Select Work Items option.
1. In the Right Panel, click on the Select Work Items option.
   A pop-up window will appear with options to add work items.
   In the pop-up window, you have two methods for adding work items:
• Query: Choose the option to add work items via a Query if you already have a predefined query or need to search for work items based on specific criteria.
• Work Item(s): If you prefer to add specific work items, use the Work Item(s) option. With this option you can also search for an specific work time by ID or Title.
2. After selecting the work items, click the OK button to add them to your mockup reference list.
   Below the work items section on the Right Panel, you will find the Fields option.
   By default, the following fields are pre-selected:
• ID
• Title
• Work Item Type
3. You can select additional fields by choosing the corresponding options, depending on the data you want to include in your mockup.
   History of Mockups
   The History Panel (the left side bar) is a shared component across the Prompt and Result tabs. It contains a user’s complete generation history of mockups and provides controls to create, find, manage, and share mockups.
   Opening / and closing the History Panel.
1. Click the Close Sidebar icon to slide out the History Panel.
• The icon works as a toggle button. This time clicking the same icon (now named as Open Sidebar) reopens the Mockup panel.
   1 .New Mockup Option
   The New Mockup Option allows the user to initiate a new mockup generation from any given point.
2. Search Option
   The Search option opens up a popup for the user to search their generated mockup. Results filter live as you type.
3. Filtering the Mockup List
• All: Shows all the Mockups within the selected tab.
• Recently Created: Shows the newest first.
• Recently Updated: Show Mockups most recently edited or regenerated.
4. Ellipsis Menu
• Each listed mockup shows a small three-dot (⋯) control. Click it to reveal actions:
   Rename — Users can use this option to rename a mockup
   Delete — This will permanently delete the mockup.
5. Mockups
• The Mockups section lists all the Mockups created by the user.
   Note: Mockups older than 30 days are moved into the Old Mockups subsection at the bottom of the list.
   Result Tab
   When the user moves to the Results tab, there are three specific panels or areas:
1. Chat with Mockup (the right panel)
2. Generated Mockup (the center panel)
3. Mockup Pages (the left panel)
   Chat with Mockup
   With the Chat with Mockup option users can:
• Examine the existing mockup, understand its layout, and regenerate it with updated screens, components, or design elements.
• Quickly enhance the page by adding new UI components, interactions, or linking existing elements.
• Rename components, adjust placements, swaps visuals, or refine styling on the page as needed.
   Generated Mockup (Center Panel)
   The generated mockup will be displayed in the Result Tab based on your inputs.
   Mockup Pages (Right Panel)
   Mockup Page right panel on the right defines and enlists the Mockup Pages. The Mockup Pages panel is expandable, and you can also hide it to allow more space to the generated mockup.
   From this panel, users can generate all the pages at once, add a page, and remove a page.
   Note: Individual pages can be generated by clicking on them. The first page cannot be removed.
   Modifying a Mockup / Making Changes to a Mockup
   When a mockup has been generated, users have the ease of making changes to the mockup and modifying it as per their requirement. They can make the changes overall as well as to specific components and texts.
1. If you need to edit a component start by clicking on it.
   it is automatically referenced in the Chat with Mockup awaiting your instructions for modification.
2. Enter the instructions to edit the component as per your requirement.
   Changes have now been made to the specific component.
   Similarly, to edit a text, the click on the Edit Text option in the center panel and edit the text directly.

title: Uploading Attachments/Files
answer:
(Copilot4DevOps — documented in the MR NextGen help — under "Home Page")

Copilot4DevOps lets you enhance AI-generated outputs by adding supporting files and web links from multiple sources. These inputs provide additional context to improve relevance and accuracy across Copilot4DevOps modules.
This capability improves contextual accuracy, relevance, and overall output quality across Copilot4DevOps modules.
Supported Sources
You can add up to 10 items in total (combined across all sources) from the following locations:
Upload Files (from your local device)
Work Item Attachments
BYOD (Bring Your Own Data)
Web Links
The same experience is available anywhere in Copilot4DevOps where document uploads are supported, especially the following areas:
Setup Elicitation
Dynamic Prompt
Generating a Diagram
SOP/Document Generator
Chat UI
Understanding Mockup UI
Upload File Popup Overview
When you click Upload File(s) or the + icon, the Upload File popup opens.
This popup allows you to upload files, select existing documents, or add web links for the AI to fetch and use as context.
Tabs in the Upload File popup
The popup contains four tabs, and you can switch between them without losing your selections.
Upload
Work Item Attachments
BYOD
Web Links
Upload
This tab is used to upload files from your local device.
Drag & drop the required file into the upload area.
OR
Click the Chose file button to browse from your device.
Supported File Types
Documents: .doc/.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .rtf, .odt
Spreadsheets/Data: .xls/.xlsx, .csv
Web/Config/Text: .html, .json, .xml, .yml/.yaml, .md, .txt
Code: .c/.cpp, .cs, .java, .js/.ts, .py, .php, .rb, .sh, .go, .tex
Images: .jpeg/.jpg, .png, .gif, .bmp, .webp, .svg
   Note: Maximum File Size Limit is 20 MB (larger files are not allowed and trigger an inline error)
Embedded images within uploaded documents are extracted and processed, and are made available as input to the AI model along with the document text.
When images are extracted, the system preserves the image order, image captions (where available), and the surrounding text, so each image stays linked to its contextual position within the document.
Work Item Attachments
This tab is used to show (and select if required) all files attached to the current work item.
Users can search the desired file from attachments, by filename.
Users can select multiple files simultaneously.
Files over 20 MB are automatically disabled and can not be selected.
BYOD (Bring Your Own Data)
The BYOD tab lets you select documents previously uploaded to your organization’s data sources.
Source Filter options:
Multi-select dropdown with the following options:
All
Team (Default)
Organization
Dropdown Logic:
Selecting All includes both Team and Organization
Selecting both Team + Organization auto-switches to All and vice-versa.
Features:
Search by filename
Multi-select
Large files (>20 MB) appear but are disabled
Images embedded within BYOD-enabled documents are also extracted and processed, and are available as input to the AI model along with their associated text.
Web Links
This tab is used to add URLs as contextual inputs.
Start by clicking + Add Links.
Provide the URL, explanatory text (optional) and then click the Add button.
The URL is added (provisionally).
Validation Rules
The system validates the URL format and accessibility
Invalid or unreachable URLs display an inline error
Invalid links cannot be added
Proceed or cancel?
When desired files are attached, click the Add File button to proceed or Cancel to close the popup without saving.
Selection Rules and Behavior
Maximum combined limit: 10 items across all sources
Selections persist when switching tabs
Each tab displays a selection count (for example: Work Item Attachments (2))
Disabled or invalid items cannot be selected
Cancel exits without applying any changes
